\section{Problem, statement and logical scope}
\begin{definition}
A \emph{gap-two representation} is a finite set
\(\calA=\{a_1<\cdots<a_t\}\subset\N_{\ge2}\) such that
\[
\sum_{a\in\calA}\frac1a=1,
\qquad a_{i+1}-a_i\le2\quad(1\le i<t).
\]
Write \(a=\min\calA\) and \(M_*=\max\calA\).
\end{definition}
Erd\H{o}s Problem 287 asks whether such a representation exists. Its usual formulation requires a gap of at least three in every distinct-denominator representation of one; the example \(1/2+1/3+1/6=1\) shows that three would be sharp \cite{FC287}. Eventual nonexistence is a weaker statement: it bounds \(M_*\), leaving a finite set of possible maxima to examine.

The purpose of this version is to make the exact analytic dependency inspectable. A supplied research sequence culminates in a proposed actual-atom estimate. Rather than cite its status labels as evidence, we state that estimate as Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:atom} and prove the consequences from it. The accompanying audit records which parts are elementary, which use published results, and which belong to the new analytic claim.

\begin{theorem}[Conditional asymptotic finiteness]\label{thm:main}
Assume Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:atom} for the fixed affine forms, coefficient atoms and smooth profiles constructed below, uniformly in the specified small base. Then there exists \(M_0\) such that every gap-two representation has \(M_*<M_0\).
\end{theorem}

The hypothesis is an estimate for exponential sums, not a hypothesis asserting the existence of prime pairs or the desired conclusion. In particular, the theorem does not assume a solution of the problem under different terminology. The manuscript supplies the source identities and the numerical consumer; the separately supplied analytic proof must still be judged on its own merits.

\paragraph{Notation.}
The variable \(M_*\) always denotes a maximum denominator. In a convolution cell we instead use \(x=MN\), where \(M,N\) are lengths. The dimension \(k\), the affine slopes and all small positive exponents are fixed before \(x\to\infty\). Write \(\e{t}=\exp(2\pi i t)\), \(\ep q t=\e{t/q}\), and extend the usual multiplicative functions in the standard way. Intervals \(n\sim N\) are dyadic; the convention can be chosen to include the integer one when \(N=1\). Constants may depend on fixed data but not on the growing base or residue. A factor \(x^{o(1)}\) is used only with a previously available fixed power saving, never to absorb an arbitrary-logarithmic error.

\section{A finite consumer with seven blocks}\label{sec:consumer}
\subsection{Harmonic placement and row rigidity}
The two elementary observations below require no sieve theory.
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:harmonic}
A gap-two representation satisfies \(a\le M_*/e+1\). Consequently \(a<3M_*/8\) for all sufficiently large \(M_*\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Since \(1\le\sum_{n=a}^{M_*}1/n\le\int_{a-1}^{M_*}\dd t/t\), we have \(M_*/(a-1)\ge e\). Also \(e>8/3\).
\end{proof}
\begin{lemma}[Bounded-cofactor exclusion]\label{lem:row}
Fix \(H\ge1\), and set
\[
L_H=\lcm(1,\ldots,H),\qquad B_H=\sum_{j=1}^H L_H/j.
\]
If \(p\) is prime, \(p>\max(H,B_H)\), and \(\lfloor M_*/p\rfloor\le H\), then a set \(\calA\subset[2,M_*]\) with integral reciprocal sum contains no multiple of \(p\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The assumptions imply \(M_*<(H+1)p\le p^2\). In the localization of \(\mathbb Z\) at \(p\), multiply the reciprocal identity by \(p\) and reduce modulo \(p\). Only selected multiples \(jp\) contribute, giving
\(\sum_{jp\in\calA}j^{-1}=0\pmod p\).
After multiplication by \(L_H\), the resulting nonnegative integer is at most \(B_H<p\), hence is zero. Every summand is positive, so the selected set of cofactors is empty.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Prescribed coefficient shape}
\begin{lemma}[Prescribed-shape realization]\label{lem:shape}
Given finitely many pairwise disjoint bounded open intervals \(J_i\subset(0,\infty)\), there are positive distinct integers \(a_i=A_0+b_i\), with the normalized offsets \(b_i/T\in J_i\), such that
\[
\gcd(a_i,a_j)=|a_i-a_j|\quad(i\ne j).
\]
The translation \(A_0\) may be taken arbitrarily large relative to the chosen offsets.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let \(s\) be the number of intervals and \(E=\binom{s}{2}\). Choose \(P_0\) sufficiently large in terms of \(E\). For every prime \(p\le P_0\), prescribe
\(b_i\equiv p^{i-1}\pmod{p^s}\).
CRT puts each \(b_i\) in a fixed progression; its intersection with \(TJ_i\) has \(\gg T\) choices as \(T\to\infty\).

For distinct unordered pairs of indices and a prime \(p>P_0\), the two equations saying that both pair differences vanish modulo \(p\) have rank two. Successively eliminating leaves in the graph of these two edges bounds the fraction of bad choices by \((1/p+1/L)^2\), where \(L\gg T\) is the smallest number of coordinate choices. Differences are \(O(T)\). Thus the union-bound cost is at most
\[
\binom E2\left(\frac1{P_0-1}+O\!\left(\frac{\log T}{L}+\frac{T}{L^2}\right)\right)<1
\]
for large \(P_0\), then large \(T\). Choose offsets for which each \(p>P_0\) divides at most one pair difference.

The congruences \(A_0\equiv-b_i\pmod{|b_j-b_i|}\) are compatible. Indeed, at a small prime,
\(v_p(b_i-b_j)=\min(i-1,j-1)\); if two moduli contain \(p^v\), all corresponding offsets are zero modulo \(p^v\). At a large prime no two moduli overlap. Generalized CRT supplies \(A_0\), and arbitrarily large positive translates are possible. The difference divides both \(a_i,a_j\), while their gcd divides the difference, proving equality.
\end{proof}

Let \(G\) be the graph on \(\mathbb Z/7\mathbb Z\) whose edges have differences \(2,3,4,5\). It is the complement of the seven-cycle and has independence number two. Blow each vertex up to an equal block. Choose disjoint narrow offset intervals near the seven positions \(1,\ldots,7\), and use Lemma~\ref{lem:shape}. For useful edges the ratio of the largest to smallest offset difference can be made arbitrarily close to \(5/2\). Taking \(A_0/T\) large makes the ratios of the products \(a_i a_j\) arbitrarily close to one. Hence the numbers
\[
\lambda_{ij}=\frac{a_i a_j}{|a_i-a_j|}
\]
over useful edges have ratio less than \(8/3\).

For \(a_i<a_j\), let \(d_{ij}=a_j-a_i=\gcd(a_i,a_j)\). The forms \(L_i(t)=a_i t+1\) satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:contact}
\frac{a_j}{d_{ij}}L_i(t)-\frac{a_i}{d_{ij}}L_j(t)=1.
\end{equation}
Choose fixed rational \(c_1,c_2>0\) with
\[
\frac3{8\lambda_{\min}}<c_1<c_2<\frac1{\lambda_{\max}}.
\]
All useful contacts for \(c_1M_*<t<c_2M_*\) are in \((3M_*/8,M_*)\) for large \(M_*\). The family is admissible, since \(t=0\) avoids every prime. Its prime values are \(>\kappa M_*\) for one fixed \(\kappa>0\).

\begin{proposition}[Moment consumer]\label{prop:consumer}
For the fixed forms and interval just constructed, suppose there are nonnegative weights on the integer parameters for every sufficiently large \(X\). Let \(Y_b\) count prime form values in block \(b\), and put
\[
P=\sum_{b=1}^7Y_b,\qquad Q_2=\sum_{b=1}^7\binom{Y_b}{2},\qquad Z=\#\{b:Y_b>0\}.
\]
If
\begin{equation}\label{eq:consumer}
(\E P)^2>2(\E P+2\E Q_2),
\end{equation}
then no sufficiently large \(M_*\) supports a gap-two representation.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Cauchy on parameter space times block index gives
\((\E P)^2\le(\E Z)\E\sum_bY_b^2=(\E Z)(\E P+2\E Q_2)\).
Thus some parameter has three occupied blocks. They contain an edge of \(G\). Equation~\eqref{eq:contact} gives adjacent physical multiples in the source by Lemma~\ref{lem:harmonic}. Their prime factors have fixed cofactor height, so Lemma~\ref{lem:row} excludes both positions. This contradicts the gap-two property between the selected endpoints.
\end{proof}

\section{The nonnegative weight and its moments}\label{sec:moments}
Fix a sufficiently small spectator-support exponent \(\delta_s>0\), and subsequently a sufficiently large fixed dimension \(k\), divisible by seven. Let \(F\) be a symmetric smooth function supported in \(\sum t_i\le\delta_s\), chosen in the standard finite-tensor class of the Maynard sieve. Write
\[
I(F)=\int F^2,\quad
J_i(F)=\int\left(\int F\dd t_i\right)^2,\quad
L_{ij}(F)=\int\left(\iint F\dd t_i\dd t_j\right)^2.
\]
The missing integration variables in each outer integral are precisely the variables already integrated inside.

The construction of Banks--Freiberg--Maynard \cite[Lemma~4.6]{BFM} gives, after choosing the scale of the simplex and then \(k\), a fixed finite-tensor function with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:functionals}
\frac{\sum_iJ_i}{I}>(1-\eta)u,
\qquad
\frac{\sum_{i<j\text{ in one block}}L_{ij}}{I}
<\frac{(1+\eta)u^2}{14},
\end{equation}
for any prescribed fixed \(u\), with arbitrarily small fixed \(\eta>0\). In that construction the individual ratios are asymptotic to \(\rho\delta_s\log k/k\) and its square; choose \(\rho\delta_s\log k=u\), with \(\rho<1\), after increasing \(k\). Finite smooth approximation is made with strict margins.

Put
\[
w=\log\log\log X,\quad W=\prod_{p\le w}p,
\quad B_X=\frac{\phi(W)}W\log X,
\quad \mathcal N_X=\frac{(c_2-c_1)X}{W}B_X^{-k}.
\]
All prime divisors of the fixed slopes and their nonzero differences eventually divide \(W\). Choose a fixed finite tensor representation
\[
F(t_1,\ldots,t_k)=\sum_{v=1}^{V}\prod_{i=1}^k f'_{i,v}(t_i),
\]
with smooth compactly supported \(f_{i,v}\), each product supported in
\(\sum_i t_i\le\delta_s\). Explicitly set
\[
\omega_{\mathbf d}=\1_{(\prod_i d_i,W)=1}
\left(\prod_{i=1}^k\mu(d_i)\right)
\sum_{v=1}^{V}\prod_{i=1}^k
f_{i,v}\!\left(\frac{\log d_i}{\log X}\right).
\]
These coefficients are bounded by a fixed constant and supported on
\(\prod_i d_i\le X^{\delta_s}\). We use
\begin{equation}\label{eq:physicalweight}
w_X(t)=\1_{c_1X<t<c_2X}\1_{W\mid t}
\left(\sum_{d_i\mid L_i(t)}\omega_{\mathbf d}\right)^2.
\end{equation}
The standard smooth-divisor calculation, with the explicit affine CRT normalization below, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:01moments}
S_0=(1+o(1))\mathcal N_XI,
\qquad S_1=(1+o(1))\mathcal N_X\sum_iJ_i.
\end{equation}
Here \(S_1=\sum_tw_X(t)P(t)\). These are applications of the smooth Euler calculation in \cite[Lemma~4.1]{Polymath8b} and ordinary Bombieri--Vinogradov, not applications of a fixed-shift theorem with the slopes relabelled.

For example, if \(p=L_j(t)\) and \(q_i\mid L_i(t)\), then
\[
p\equiv1-a_ja_i^{-1}\pmod{q_i},\qquad
p\equiv1\pmod{a_jW}.
\]
All residues are units and the correspondence with \(t\) is bijective. The complete modulus is \(a_jW\prod_{i\ne j}q_i\), strictly below one-half. Also
\begin{equation}\label{eq:slopecancel}
\phi(a_jW)=a_j\phi(W),
\end{equation}
so the fixed interval dilation cancels exactly. Outside \(W\), roots belonging to distinct coordinates are distinct; incompatible shared divisors contribute zero. Extracting the zeta factors leaves local corrections \(1+O_k(p^{-2})\), whose tail product tends to one. This proves that the same integrals occur in \eqref{eq:01moments}.

\section{A full parity-sensitive scalar upper weight}\label{sec:scalar}
Let \(e_0=1/T\) be a sufficiently small fixed reciprocal integer, let \(\tau=e_0^9\), and set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:internallevel}
D_{\rm tot}=X^{59/100},\quad
D=D_{\rm tot}^{1/(1+e_0+\tau)},\quad
u_0=D^{e_0^2},\quad D_{\rm low}=D^{e_0}=X^\beta.
\end{equation}
Use disjoint geometric prime intervals \(I_h=(P_h,P_h^{1+\tau}]\), beginning at \(u_0\), with a consistent endpoint convention. The ordinary rounded upper-box family consists of nonincreasing vectors \(\mathbf P=(P_1,\ldots,P_J)\) satisfying, for every odd \(i\le J\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:oddprefix}
\Bigl(\prod_{h<i}P_h\Bigr)P_i^3<
\begin{cases}D,&J\text{ even},\\D^{1/(1+\tau)},&J\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
The empty vector is included. For each vector define the labelled distinct-prime count \(T_{\mathbf P}(a)\), its repeated-bin multiplicity \(\gamma(\mathbf P)=\prod_I m_I!\), and the squarefree product indicator
\(B_{\mathbf P}=T_{\mathbf P}/\gamma(\mathbf P)\).

Let \(\lambda_{\rm low}^{+},\lambda_{\rm low}^{-}\) be the upper and lower fundamental-lemma weights of level \(D_{\rm low}\) on the allowed primes at most \(u_0\). Put
\[
\kappa_J=\begin{cases}\lambda_{\rm low}^{+},&J\text{ even},\\
\lambda_{\rm low}^{-},&J\text{ odd},\end{cases}
\]
and define the full coefficient by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fullweight}
\ell_X(d)=\sum_{J,\mathbf P}(-1)^J
\sum_{ba=d}\kappa_J(b)B_{\mathbf P}(a).
\end{equation}
All primes dividing \(W\) are omitted from the sieve prime set. In particular the \(J=0\) term is the entire low upper weight, not merely \(\1_{d=1}\). The coefficients and the parity convention are read from the signed remainder in the fundamental-lemma construction \cite[Section~5]{Lichtman}, not from an ambiguous shorthand for \(\mathcal D^{(J)}\).

\begin{lemma}[Support and positivity]\label{lem:scalar}
The full coefficient is squarefree, bounded under the normalized bin convention, and supported on \(d\le X^{59/100}\). Its divisor multiplier
\(U_X(v)=\sum_{d\mid v}\ell_X(d)\) is nonnegative and majorizes the prime event for \(v\asymp X\). For a dimension-one local density with a uniform upper dimension constant, its model mean satisfies the usual upper-linear-sieve estimate with internal level \(D\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The low/high prime decomposition of \(d\) and its high bin vector are unique. Equation~\eqref{eq:oddprefix} implies the upper-endpoint odd-prefix inequalities at level \(D^{1+\tau}\), hence the high product is at most \(D^{1+\tau}\). Multiplication by \(b\le D^{e_0}\) proves the total support bound.

For positivity, first use the upper Rosser expansion on the high prime set. Rounding enlarges positive even-parity contributions and restricts negative odd-parity contributions, so preserves its pointwise upper property. Multiply by the indicator of avoidance of the low primes. In each even high-parity term substitute the pointwise low upper sieve; in each odd term substitute the low lower sieve before multiplying by the negative sign. Each substitution increases the expression. The result is exactly \(U_X\), and is at least the indicator of avoidance of all relevant primes, hence is nonnegative.

The model mean is evaluated in the same signed construction: the low factors give their fundamental-lemma means, with exponentially small error in \(1/e_0\); the rounded high-box error is \(O(e_0)\) in the linear-sieve main function. This is the ordinary construction in \cite[Theorem~2.10 and Section~5]{Lichtman}, without the modified-star exclusions. There is no added constant coefficient in this argument.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Internal level is not total support]
The leading normalized coefficient is \(2\log X/\log D\), not \(2\log X/\log D_{\rm tot}\) at a fixed \(e_0\). There is ample room to retain the inflation. If \(e_0+\tau\le10^{-3}\) and the remaining total error is at most \(1/295\), then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:scalarreserve}
\frac{200}{59}(1+10^{-3})+\frac1{295}
=\frac{17}{5}-\frac1{295}<\frac{17}{5}.
\end{equation}
The unspecified constant in \(O(e_0)\) is not assigned a numerical value: first fix a permissible dimension constant, then choose \(e_0\) sufficiently small. This is an asymptotic choice, not an effective bound.

One can evaluate the scalar construction at \(z=\sqrt D\), where its parameter is \(s=2\). All high primes in \eqref{eq:oddprefix} are less than \(D^{(1+\tau)/3}<\sqrt D\) for small \(\tau\). Thus the coefficient is unchanged when the target cutoff is increased to \(X^{1/2}\); the larger roughness event is a subset of the one already majorized. This avoids silently using a construction written only for \(s\ge2\) at \(s<2\).
\end{remark}

\subsection{Collision-preserving model comparison}
Fix designated coordinates \(j\ne l\) and restrict their divisor coordinates to one. Denote the remaining amplitude by \(A_{jl}(t)\). Outside \(W\), conditional on absence of the \(j\)-root, the other roots occupy distinct classes among \(p-1\) possibilities. Conditional further on every spectator root state, the \(l\)-root probability is zero if a spectator root is present, and otherwise is
\[
q_p=\frac1{p-k+1}=:h_p.
\]
For any nonnegative Boolean function \(U\),
\[
\frac{\E_qU}{\prod_p(1-q_p)}
=\sum_S U(S)\prod_{p\in S}\frac{q_p}{1-q_p}
\]
is increasing in every \(q_p\). Consequently the scalar upper mean for \(h_p\) bounds the conditional mean, including the exact factor \(\prod(1-q_p)\). Multiplying by the full spectator square and averaging yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:collision}
\E_j[A_{jl}^2U_X]\le
(F_{\rm lin}(2)+O(e_0))\,V_j(\sqrt D)\,\E_{jl}[A_{jl}^2],
\end{equation}
where \(V_j(z)=\prod_{w<p<z}(1-1/(p-1))\).

For \(w\) sufficiently large in terms of fixed \(k\), \(h_p=p^{-1}+O_k(p^{-2})\) satisfies the dimension-one upper condition with a uniform constant: the additional logarithm of the Euler ratio above any \(v\ge w\) is \(O(k/v)\). Conditioning on absence of both designated roots gives local probabilities \(1/(p-2)\). Their smooth quadratic Euler factors differ from the standard ones by \(1+O_k(p^{-2})\), giving
\[
\E_{jl}[A_{jl}^2]=B_X^{-(k-2)}(L_{jl}(F)+o(1)).
\]
Combining this with \eqref{eq:slopecancel} and \(V_j(\sqrt D)\) gives the pair main coefficient in \eqref{eq:scalarreserve}. All cancellation occurs inside the full square; no termwise positivity is asserted for signed divisor coefficients.

\section{Exact squarefree export and its ranges}\label{sec:export}
\subsection{A constant-variation squarefree projector}
Fix a box vector and a partition of its labelled positions into three groups. If a bin \(I\) has \(m_I\) positions, let \(m_{I,i}\) be the number assigned to group \(i\), and put
\[
C_{\mathbf P}=\prod_I\binom{m_I}{m_{I,1},m_{I,2},m_{I,3}}.
\]
Independently colour every allowed high prime with one of three colours. For a colouring \(\chi\), let \(\gamma_{i,\chi}\) indicate squarefree products having the prescribed bin counts and using only colour \(i\). Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:colour}
B_{\mathbf P}(a)=\frac{3^J}{C_{\mathbf P}}
\E_\chi[(\gamma_{1,\chi}*\gamma_{2,\chi}*\gamma_{3,\chi})(a)]
\end{equation}
for every integer \(a\). For a squarefree allowed product, the probability of the prescribed counts is \(C_{\mathbf P}/3^J\); a repeated prime is excluded either inside a squarefree factor or by disjoint colours. This proves the identity also on nonsquarefree arguments.

Let \(G_{1,J,\chi}=\kappa_J*\gamma_{1,\chi}\). Its low/high factorization is unique, so \(|G_{1,J,\chi}|\le1\). Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tensor}
\ell_X=\sum_{J,\mathbf P}(-1)^J\frac{3^J}{C_{\mathbf P}}
\E_\chi[G_{1,J,\chi}*\gamma_{2,\chi}*\gamma_{3,\chi}].
\end{equation}
The total variation is a fixed constant after the scalar parameters are fixed. It is not the number of possible colourings. Apply this identity to the linear centered remainder before Cauchy. It does not authorize omission of cross terms in an already squared sum.

For sufficiently large \(X\), every high prime exceeds
\(z_0=X^{1/(\log\log X)^3}\). Hence the high variable factors have no nontrivial \(z_0\)-smooth part. The regular-source cutoff obeys
\(\sm(fd;z_0)=\sm(fb;z_0)\), and is unary in the common factor \(bq_1\). Restrictions \((d,fAB)=1\) split into unary factor masks.

\subsection{The actual support test}
Fix \(0<\kappa<10^{-5}\), take \(\beta<\kappa/100\), and put
\[
N'=Nx^{-2\beta},\qquad D_*=x^{3/5-50\kappa}.
\]
We use only cells with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:criticalinterval}
x^{3\kappa}\le N\le x^{1/3+\kappa/2}.
\end{equation}
Then \(x^{2\kappa}\le N'\le x^{1/3+\kappa}\). For each high box, its ordered real upper endpoints \(U_i=P_i^{1+\tau}\) satisfy
\[
\Bigl(\prod_{h<i}U_h\Bigr)U_i^3\le D^{1+\tau}<x^{59/100}<D_*
\quad(i\text{ odd}).
\]
This verifies the full odd-prefix support, not merely the total size.

Pascadi's allocation argument \cite[Proposition~5.2]{Pascadi} uses order and multiplicative comparisons and therefore applies to these real endpoints. Its three terminal alternatives give the caps below, with \(N'\) in place of \(N\):
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}clll@{}}\toprule
Case & Common factor & Second factor & Third factor\\\midrule
I & \(N'x^{-\kappa}\) & \(x^{1/5-5\kappa}\) & \(x^{1/3+2\kappa}/N'\)\\
II & \(N'x^{-\kappa}\) & \(U\) & \(x^{3/5-3\kappa}/(N'U)\)\\
III & \(N'x^{-\kappa}\) & \(x^{3/5-3\kappa}/(N'V)\) & \(V\)\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
In II, \(x^{1/5-5\kappa}<U\le x^{4/15-5\kappa}\); in III,
\(x^{1/3+2\kappa}<N'V\le x^{2/5+2\kappa}\).
The allocation is fixed on the whole box by applying the argument to upper endpoints. Missing prime positions are padded by one, not by fictitious primes.

Each row implies
\(N'^2q_2q_3^2\le x^{1-\kappa}\) and
\(N'^2q_2^5q_3^2\le x^{2-\kappa}\).
Inserting \(b\le x^\beta\) in the common factor gives
\begin{align}
Q_1&\le Nx^{-\kappa-\beta},\label{eq:range1}\\
N^2Q_2Q_3^2&\le x^{1-\kappa+4\beta},\label{eq:range2}\\
N^2Q_2^5Q_3^2&\le x^{2-\kappa+4\beta}.\label{eq:range3}
\end{align}
Under \(Q=Q_1,R=Q_3,S=Q_2\), the three spectral margins are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:margins}
\kappa-4\beta,\qquad
\frac{71}{100}(\kappa-4\beta),\qquad
\frac{36\kappa-89\beta}{25}.
\end{equation}
For the middle inequality use
\[
(N^2Q_2Q_3^2)^{21/50}(N^2Q_2^5Q_3^2)^{29/100}
=N^{71/50}Q_2^{187/100}Q_3^{71/50}
\ge N^{71/50}RS^{93/50}.
\]
Choose the kernel parameter \(\varepsilon=\kappa/2000\). All required reserves survive fixed dyadic constants. This is an explicit factor-support argument; no coarse product bound is substituted for it.

\section{Relative arithmetic progressions and original-source pruning}\label{sec:relative}
Fix \(j\ne l\). For a compatible paired spectator tuple \(\xi\), write
\[
q_i=[d_i,d_i'],\quad q_0=\prod_{i\ne j,l}q_i,\quad
f_\xi=a_jWq_0,\quad \Gamma_\xi=\omega_{\mathbf d}\omega_{\mathbf d'}.
\]
The \(q_i\) are squarefree, pairwise coprime, coprime to \(W\), and \(q_0\le X^{2\delta_s}\). Let \(J_j(X)=(a_jc_1X+1,a_jc_2X+1)\), and define
\[
P_j(q,b)=\#\{p\in J_j(X)\cap\Pp:p\equiv b\pmod q\},\qquad
E_j(q,b)=P_j(q,b)-\frac{V_j(X)}{\phi(q)},
\]
where \(V_j\) is the corresponding \(\Li\)-difference.
The actual residue satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:actualcrt}
b\equiv c_\xi\pmod{f_\xi},\qquad
 a_l b\equiv a_l-a_j\pmod d.
\end{equation}
It is a unit, and \((d,f_\xi)=1\). The same \(q_0\) may carry several labelled residues; none is suppressed.

\begin{lemma}[Relative centering]\label{lem:recenter}
For \((f,d)=1\), with \(b\equiv c\pmod f\),
\[
E_j(fd,b)=
\left[P_j(fd,b)-\frac{P_j(f,c)}{\phi(d)}\right]
+\frac{E_j(f,c)}{\phi(d)}.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Expand both terms and use \(\phi(fd)=\phi(f)\phi(d)\).
\end{proof}

For fixed \(k\), each prime of \(q_0\) chooses one of \(k-2\) coordinates and one of first/second/both statuses. Thus the number of paired allocations is at most \((3(k-2))^{\omega(q_0)}\), before restrictions. It follows, without cancellation, that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:packetnorm}
\sum_\xi\frac{|\Gamma_\xi|\tau(f_\xi)^D}{\phi(f_\xi)}
\ll_{k,F,D}(\log X)^{C_{k,F,D}}.
\end{equation}
The Euler product proving this is \(\prod_{p\le X^{2\delta_s}}(1+C/(p-1))\). This is a positive logarithmic power, not the signed inverse-log main normalization.

Ordinary BV with a maximum over unit residues, followed by divisor-weighted Cauchy, pays
\begin{equation}\label{eq:basepayment}
\sum_{j<l}\sum_\xi\Gamma_\xi E_j(f_\xi,c_\xi)
\sum_{\substack{d\le X^{.59}\ (d,f_\xi)=1}}
\frac{\ell_X(d)}{\phi(d)}=o(\mathcal N_XI).
\end{equation}
Indeed the inner reciprocal sum is a fixed logarithmic power; the bases are \(X^{2\delta_s+o(1)}\), strictly below one-half; all preimages have divisor-power multiplicity. Request the BV exponent larger than the fixed tensor and normalization losses.

\begin{lemma}[Original large-smooth sector]\label{lem:smooth}
Let \(z_0=X^{1/(\log\log X)^3}\) and \(y_0=X^{1/\log\log X}\). The part of the original remainder with \(\sm(f_\xi d;z_0)\ge y_0\) has total absolute contribution \(O_A(X/(\log X)^A)\), for every fixed \(A\). The growing-squarefull part is eventually empty.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write \(f_\xi d=a_jWR\). Then \(R\) is squarefree and coprime to \(W\), so \(\sq(f_\xi d)=a_j\rad(a_j)\) eventually. For the smooth sector, \(a_jW\le y_0^{1/2}\), hence \(\sm(R;z_0)\ge y_0^{1/2}\). All full moduli are at most \(X^{.5901}\); uniformly in residues, trivial interval counting gives \(|E_j(Q,b)|\ll X/\phi(Q)\).

With \(C\) dominating the per-prime preimages, Rankin's trick with \(t=1/\log z_0\) bounds the remaining reciprocal sum by
\[
y_0^{-t/2}
\prod_{p\le X^{.5901}}
\left(1+\frac{C p^{t\1_{p\le z_0}}}{p-1}\right)
\ll
\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12(\log\log X)^2\right)(\log X)^{C'}.
\]
This beats every fixed logarithmic power, including the normalization. This concerns the original moduli only; gcds created after squaring are not deleted by this lemma.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Relative BDH as an orthogonal projection}
For a SW sequence \(\alpha_n\), define, for \((f,q)=1\),
\[
\Delta_\alpha^{f,c}(q,a)=
\sum_{\substack{n\sim N\ n\equiv c\ (f)}}
\alpha_n\left(\1_{n\equiv a\ (q)}-\frac{\1_{(n,q)=1}}{\phi(q)}\right).
\]
If \(b_{c,a}\) is the CRT residue modulo \(fq\), then
\[
\Delta_\alpha^{f,c}(q,a)=
\Delta_\alpha(fq,b_{c,a})-
\frac1{\phi(q)}\sum_{a'\bmod q}^{*}\Delta_\alpha(fq,b_{c,a'}).
\]
Subtracting a vector mean contracts its squared norm. Summing over \(c,a\), and then over factorizations \(s=fq\), gives the following consequence of \cite[Lemma~13.8]{MaynardI}:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:RBDH}
\sum_{f\le F}\tau(f)^D\sum_c^*
\sum_{\substack{q\le Q\\(q,f)=1}}\tau(q)^D\sum_a^*
|\Delta_\alpha^{f,c}(q,a)|^2
\ll_A\frac{N^2}{(\log N)^A},
\quad FQ\le\frac{N}{(\log N)^C}.
\end{equation}
Only a larger fixed divisor exponent is required. This is not a packetwise \(L^1\) estimate.

\section{Exhaustive convolution routing and its repair}\label{sec:noncritical}
The earlier noncritical estimate was written for two lengths at least \(x^{3/8}\), whereas \eqref{eq:criticalinterval} ends near \(x^{1/3}\). This mismatch must be repaired, not hidden by the word ``noncritical.''

Use Heath--Brown's identity with three truncated M\"obius variables and three smooth variables, and dyadically decompose them. The correct alternating coefficient is \((-1)^{j-1}\binom3j\); a sign misprint in a displayed version of the identity is not used. Each M\"obius variable has length at most a fixed multiple of \(x^{1/3}\).

\begin{lemma}[Exhaustive length trichotomy]\label{lem:trichotomy}
Up to fixed endpoint factors, each six-variable cell either has an individual variable in \eqref{eq:criticalinterval}, or has one large smooth variable with short product \(U\ll x^{15\kappa}\), or has two large smooth variables with \(U\ll x^{12\kappa}\). In the last case each long length exceeds \(x^{1/3+\kappa/2}\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
If there is no individual length in the critical interval, every length is either below \(x^{3\kappa}\) or above \(x^{1/3+\kappa/2}\). The M\"obius lengths must be in the first class. At most two of the smooth lengths can be in the second, since three would have product greater than \(x\). At least one is large, since \(18\kappa<1\). Five or four remaining small variables give the claimed bounds. Fixed factors are absorbed using the strict endpoint reserves.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Rough SW input}
The selected critical variable carries either \(1\), \(\mu\), or a logarithm, restricted to \(P^-(n)>z_0\). Such a restriction does not follow from a residue-mask preservation rule. Here is a direct justification. For small test moduli, approximate the roughness indicator by upper/lower fundamental-lemma weights at level \(N^{1/4}\). Their positive gap has mean \(\ll N\exp(-c\log N/\log z_0)+N^{1/4}(\log N)^C\), smaller than every fixed negative logarithmic power. With a M\"obius coefficient, on \(d\mid n\), write
\(\mu(dm)=\mu(d)\mu(m)\1_{(d,m)=1}\).
The progression modulus for \(m\) is still the test modulus, not its product with \(d\). Ordinary SW for \(\mu\), with the additional coprimality modulus, can therefore be summed using
\(\sum_{d\le N^{1/4}}\tau(d)^C/d\ll(\log N)^{C'}\).
The sequence \(1\) is simpler; logarithms follow by partial summation. For test moduli larger than a sufficiently high logarithmic power, trivial progression and totient bounds give the SW condition. Thus the full relative-BDH input is available uniformly at every fixed positive-power length in \eqref{eq:criticalinterval}. No fixed residue restriction is asserted to preserve ordinary SW.

\subsection{One large factor}
Let \(UT\asymp x\), \(U\le x^{.01}\), and let \(T\) be the long rough smooth-variable length. A fundamental-lemma progression estimate gives, uniformly in unit residues and \(Q\le x^{.5901}\),
\[
\text{rough progression error}\ll_A\frac{T}{Q(\log x)^A},\qquad T\ge Qx^{\eta_0}.
\]
The unit-restricted principal term is retained. Primes dividing \(Q\) but not already removed by roughness exceed \(z_0\); their correction is \(\ll T\tau(Q)/(\phi(Q)z_0)\), with negligible endpoint terms. Summing the short variable and all divisor-bounded source preimages uses \(\sum_Q\tau(Q)^C/Q\ll(\log x)^{C'}\). This preserves the true reciprocal density \cite[Lemma~5.4]{MaynardII}.

\subsection{Two large factors below the old \(3/8\) threshold}
The smooth two-divisor proof of \cite[Lemma~7.1]{MaynardII} is uniform in the unit residue and gives, before range simplification,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:twofactor}
|\mathscr D(Q,b)|\ll x^{o(1)}
\left(\frac{x}{QN_1}+UQ^{1/2}\right),\qquad N_1\le N_2,\quad UN_1N_2\asymp x.
\end{equation}
It needs the long lengths to exceed a small fixed power, not \(x^{3/8}\). Lemma~\ref{lem:trichotomy} gives \(N_i>x^{1/3+\kappa/2}\) and \(U<x^{.01}\), so the printed range \(Q\le x^{2/3-2\eta_0}/U^{2/3}\) has ample reserve. Summing actual preimages gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:twosum}
\sum_{Q\le x^{.5901}}\tau(Q)^C|\mathscr D(Q,b_Q)|
\ll x^{2/3-\kappa/2+o(1)}+x^{17903/20000+o(1)}=o(x).
\end{equation}
No fixed-residue assumption is inserted into this estimate.

For rough long variables, use fundamental-lemma upper and lower multipliers \(U_i\ge I_i\ge L_i\), with divisor support \(x^{o(1)}\). The pointwise sandwich
\[
L_1U_2+U_1L_2-U_1U_2\le I_1I_2\le U_1U_2
\]
reduces the count to \eqref{eq:twofactor}, with an \(x^{o(1)}\) enlargement of \(U\). The principal upper/lower gap has reciprocal \(1/Q\) density. Smooth upper/lower rectangles similarly treat product endpoints; their total principal boundary mass is \(O(x/(Q\log^B x))\), and their errors retain the power margin in \eqref{eq:twosum}. Thus the previously uncovered length region is genuinely handled.

\subsection{Prime powers}
The replacement of prime indicators by \(\Lambda/\log\) is made in the original source before tensorization. For a prime power \(v\asymp X\), the base and affine congruences force the spectator divisors to divide the actual fixed affine values, and \(d\) divides \(a_l v-a_l+a_j\). Each such \(v\) has only \(X^{o(1)}\) source preimages, by divisor bounds for finitely many fixed linear forms. There are \(O(X^{1/2}\log X)\) proper prime powers. Their total physical contribution is \(X^{1/2+o(1)}\); the model part is bounded by the same prime-power count times a fixed reciprocal-modulus logarithmic sum. It is not estimated by multiplying a residue-uniform error by \(X^{.59}\).

\section{The critical reduction before the new analytic hypothesis}\label{sec:ordering}
We record the parts needed to connect the original remainder to the actual atom. This also fixes the normalization of the hypothesis.

For a separated cell, write the full scalar divisor as \(lr\), with \((l,r)=1\), and retain the physical base \(f\). Set
\[
I_s(v)=\1_{Av\equiv B\ (s)},\quad
U_s(v)=\frac{\1_{(v,s)=1}}{\phi(s)},\quad h_s=I_s-U_s.
\]
The exact identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:telescoping}
I_{lr}-U_{lr}=I_lh_r+h_lU_r
\end{equation}
is used before Cauchy. The second term is a relative small-modulus discrepancy. If \(\alpha^{(r)}_n=\alpha_n\1_{(n,r)=1}\), its SW condition costs only \(\tau(r)^C\), since the extra coprimality modulus in the definition is replaced by its product with \(r\).

For fixed coprime \(f,l\), the map
\[
m\mapsto(c\overline m\bmod f,\ B\overline{Am}\bmod l)
\]
has at most \(M/(fl)+1\) preimages per pair of unit residues. The range export gives \(fL\le Nx^{-\eta_1}\) and \(M\gg fL\). Cauchy in \(m,l\) consequently bounds the centering term, for fixed \(r,f\), by
\[
\frac{M(\log x)^C}{\phi(r)}
\sqrt{\frac{\mathscr R_r(f)}{f}},
\]
where \(\mathscr R_r(f)\) is the complete relative BDH energy. Cauchy across the packets, using \eqref{eq:packetnorm}, and then \eqref{eq:RBDH}, pays the whole centering family. This is a single family estimate; there is no packet-count multiplier on a logarithmic error.

For the first term of \eqref{eq:telescoping}, Cauchy while the base is still present gives
\[
|T_\xi|^2\le\mathcal B_\xi V_\xi,\qquad
\mathcal B_\xi\ll ML(\log x)^C,
\]
where
\[
V_\xi=\sum_{l,m}\Psi(m/M)
\left|\sum_{r,n}c_{\xi,l,r}\alpha_n
\1_{mn\equiv c\ (f)}I_l(mn)h_r(mn)\right|^2.
\]
Both copies satisfy \(n_1\equiv n_2\pmod{fl}\).

\subsection{Zero covariance and the mixed term}
Put \(g=(r_1,r_2)\) and \(t=[r_1,r_2]\). Averaging the full periodic summand over its period gives exactly
\begin{equation}\label{eq:zerocov}
\frac1{flt}\left(\1_{n_1\equiv n_2\ (g)}-\frac1{\phi(g)}\right).
\end{equation}
For \(g=1\) it vanishes termwise. For \(g>1\), roughness implies \(g>z_0\), and residue counting, together with the number \(O(R^2/g^2)\) of pairs having that gcd, bounds the zero contribution by
\[
(\log x)^C\left(\frac{MN^2}{f^2Lz_0}+\frac{MN}{f}\right).
\]
After outer Cauchy this is \((x/f)(\log x)^C(z_0^{-1/2}+\sqrt{fL/N})\), summable by \eqref{eq:packetnorm}.

For fixed smooth \(\Psi\), the lattice discrepancy satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lattice}
\left|\sum_{m\equiv a\ (q)}\Psi(m/T)-\frac{T}{q}\int\Psi\right|
\le\Var(\Psi)
\end{equation}
for all \(q,T>0\). Compare the value and integral on each lattice cell to prove this. The complete actual--model M\"obius expansion has a factor \(1/\phi(r_2)\) and divisors \(k\mid r_2\). Applying \eqref{eq:lattice} to the full nonzero Fourier series before taking absolute values gives
\[
|F_{AB,\xi}|\ll(\log x)^C\left(\frac{RN^2}{f}+LRN\right).
\]
Since \(fLR\le x^{.5901}\), \(M\ge x^{5/8}\), and \(fL\le Nx^{-\eta_1}\), its square-root-normalized family has a fixed power saving. The exact change \(m=km'\) gives the same conclusion but is not required to invoke a separate mixed spectral theorem.

\subsection{The nonclean actual--actual terms}
The same physical divisor-count argument removes common \(r\)-factors: a common \(g\) forces both \(n_1\equiv n_2\pmod{flg}\) and one \(m\)-class modulo \(flg\). For fixed physical variables, the residual divisor choices are bounded by
\(\tau(Amn_1-B)\tau(Amn_2-B)\).
The divisor-in-progressions estimate \cite[Lemma~6.1]{MaynardII} applies since its progression modulus is at most \(x^{3/8+.5901}\), smaller than the physical length by a fixed power. It gives the same bound as after \eqref{eq:zerocov}. Exact diagonal terms cost \((x/f)\sqrt{fL/N}\) after Cauchy. Common \(n\)-factors are handled identically, using the retained rough \(n\)-support.

For \(0<|n_1-n_2|\le H=N/(\log x)^J\), summing by the nonzero difference gives at most \(2NH/(fl)\) pairs. Divisor-weighted Cauchy and the same progression estimate give a square-root cost \((x/f)(\log x)^{-J/2+C}\). Choose \(J\) after the fixed normalization losses. The model--model endpoint term is bounded by
\((\log x)^C(N^2/f+LN)\), again giving a fixed power saving after Cauchy.

Thus, after these operations, the only nonzero term is the cleaned actual--actual sum, with
\((r_1,r_2)=(n_1,n_2)=1\), the original own-factor coprimalities, and the difference cutoff. These estimates are applied to each exact coefficient atom at its stated uniform range, not by relabelling a previously fixed quadratic expression.

\section{The actual-atom hypothesis}\label{sec:atom}
The following is the new analytic statement proposed in the accompanying research report. It is stated in full enough detail to prevent a fixed-residue theorem being silently substituted for the actual source.

\begin{hypothesis}[Uniform actual-atom estimate]\label{hyp:atom}
Fix coprime integers \(A>0,B\ne0\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and smooth profiles. Put \(x=MN\), and suppose \(Q,R,S\ge1\), \(N\ge x^\varepsilon\), \(Q\le N\), and
\begin{align*}
N^2R^2S&\le x^{1-8\varepsilon},\\
N^{71/50}RS^{93/50}&\le x^{1-16\varepsilon},\\
N^{39/25}Q^{11/25}R^2S^5&\le x^{2-32\varepsilon}.
\end{align*}
Let \(f\le x^\sigma\), \(\sigma\le\varepsilon/100\), and \((c,f)=1\). The \(q,r,s\) sequences are one-bounded and have pairwise disjoint prime supports as in \eqref{eq:tensor}; the small-prime factor belongs to the common \(q\)-sequence. All restrictions \((qrs,ABf)=1\) are unary. Empty groups are supported at one.

For \(q\sim Q,r_i\sim R,s_i\sim S,n_i\sim N\), retain
\[
\begin{gathered}
n_1\equiv n_2\pmod{fq},\quad (n_1,n_2)=1,\quad
(n_1n_2,Afq)=1,\\
(n_1,r_1s_1)=(n_2,r_2s_2)=1,\quad
(r_1s_1,r_2s_2)=1,\\
|n_1-n_2|>N/(\log x)^J,
\end{gathered}
\]
and the global cross-coprime mask supplied in Section~\ref{sec:cross}. Let \(\rho\) be the complete CRT residue modulo \(\mathfrak L=fq r_1s_1r_2s_2\) defined by
\[
n_1\rho\equiv c\pmod f,\quad
An_1\rho\equiv B\pmod{qr_1s_1},\quad
An_2\rho\equiv B\pmod{r_2s_2}.
\]
With the actual product coefficients \(C_{12}\), define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:K}
\mathcal K=
\sum\frac{C_{12}}{q r_1r_2s_1s_2}
\sum_{h\ne0}\widehat\Psi(hM/\mathfrak L)\ep{\mathfrak L}{h\rho}.
\end{equation}
The assertion is the uniform bound
\begin{equation}\label{eq:atomestimate}
|\mathcal K|\ll
f^{263/128}\frac{N^2}{Qx^\varepsilon},
\end{equation}
including the actual smooth-separated components, bounded Fourier blocks and factors equal to one. Constants may depend on the fixed data and controlled smooth seminorms, but not on \(f,c\) or the prime-colouring choices.
\end{hypothesis}

\begin{remark}[What is and is not attributed to the literature]
Pascadi \cite[Theorem~1.3(ii)]{Pascadi} establishes the \(3/5\) exponent for the specified upper-linear-sieve weights with a fixed integer residue. His Lemma~4.2 is a precise reciprocal-sum theorem with prescribed coefficient, coprimality and phase conditions. Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:atom}, with the full affine projector, is not its printed statement. The supplied actual-atom manuscript proposes a proof through a positive \(W_4\) majorant and claims the stronger bound \(f^{199/128}N^2/(Qx^{2\varepsilon})\). This paper does not turn a reported referee status into a theorem; the hypothesis remains explicit in this version.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The exact phase, retained for verification}
Put \(u=r_1s_1,v=r_2s_2\). Under the stated conditions,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:affinephase}
\begin{split}
\ep{fquv}{h\rho}
={}&\e{\frac{Bh}{An_1fquv}}\,
\ep{n_1v}{Bh(n_1-n_2)\overline{Af n_2qu}}\\
&\times\ep{Af}{h(Ac-B)\overline{qun_1v}}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
To verify it, write \(An_1\rho=B+quk\), solve for \(k\) modulo \(n_1v\) and \(Af\), and apply CRT. No cancellation of \(A\) modulo \(f\) is involved. This identity does not by itself prove \eqref{eq:atomestimate}.

\subsection{Normalization}
The physical relation is \(F_{AA}^{\sharp}=(M/f)\mathcal K\), and the original Cauchy factor is \(\mathcal B_\xi\ll MQ(\log x)^C\). Therefore \eqref{eq:atomestimate} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:normalization}
\sqrt{\mathcal B_\xi|F_{AA,\xi}^{\sharp}|}
\ll\frac{x}{f}\,f^{391/256}x^{-\varepsilon/2}(\log x)^C.
\end{equation}
The exponent is derived, not assigned:
\(\tfrac12(263/128-1)+1=391/256\).
Choose \(\sigma\) before the dimension so that \((391/256)\sigma<\varepsilon/2\), with fixed reserve. Equation~\eqref{eq:packetnorm} then sums the atom errors; finite scalar-box variation and logarithmic dyadic costs are harmless.

\section{Cross-coprime partition and ordering}\label{sec:cross}
For the cleaned source consider pairs \((u,v)=(n_1r_2s_2,n_2)\). They are coprime, polynomially bounded, and each has \(O((\log\log x)^3)\) prime factors, because all their primes exceed \(z_0\). Hence Maynard's partition lemma \cite[Lemma~13.2]{MaynardI} applies.

For completeness, independently colour each relevant prime red or blue. A pair whose combined number of distinct prime factors is at most \(D\) has probability at least \(2^{-D}\) of putting all primes of \(u\) in red and all primes of \(v\) in blue. There are polynomially many pairs. A union bound shows that \(O(2^D\log x)\) colourings cover all pairs. Assign each pair to its first successful colouring. Within a part, every first coordinate is coprime to every second coordinate. The number of parts is \(x^{o(1)}\).

This partition is made \emph{after} the relative-centering, original-source pruning, zero-mode and near-diagonal errors have been paid. It multiplies only the fixed-power error in \eqref{eq:normalization}. There is no step of the form \(x^{o(1)}(\log x)^{-A}=o(1)\) without a genuine power reserve.

\section{Completion of the conditional theorem}\label{sec:finish}
Starting from the scalar majorant, the pair sum is bounded by its model main term plus the literal prime discrepancy. Sections~\ref{sec:relative}--\ref{sec:noncritical} pay the original-source and noncritical terms, including the formerly uncovered two-large range. Section~\ref{sec:ordering} reduces the critical source to the actual cleaned \(AA\) family. Under Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:atom}, Sections~\ref{sec:atom}--\ref{sec:cross} give
\[
R_\Sigma^P(X)=o(\mathcal N_X I).
\]
All normalizations use the same \(S_0\) from \eqref{eq:physicalweight}. By \eqref{eq:collision}, \eqref{eq:scalarreserve} and \eqref{eq:functionals}, choose \(u=10^6\), \(\eta=10^{-6}\), with strict approximation margins. Then
\[
\liminf\E P\ge999999,
\qquad
\limsup\E Q_2\le\frac{1700001700000}{7}.
\]
Exact arithmetic gives
\[
\frac{999999^2}{2}-999999-2\frac{1700001700000}{7}
=\frac{199965200021}{14}>0.
\]
For every sufficiently large \(X\), inequality~\eqref{eq:consumer} follows. Proposition~\ref{prop:consumer} proves Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.

\paragraph{Order of choices.}
Fix the critical range reserve \(\kappa\); choose the scalar parameter so \(\beta<\kappa/100\); choose the atom reserve \(\varepsilon\); choose spectator support small enough for \eqref{eq:normalization}; then choose the fixed dimension and finite-tensor function; then the slopes and interval. Only afterwards let \(X\to\infty\). Fixed logarithmic losses may depend on the dimension. Fixed-power losses may not be assumed to vanish by changing an exponent already fixed earlier.

\section{Effectivity, finite computation and publication scope}\label{sec:effectivity}
Even after a proof of Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:atom} is accepted, Theorem~\ref{thm:main} is an existential asymptotic result. It does not supply a numerical \(M_0\), nor cover maxima below it.

For fixed contact data, an arithmetic threshold can be stated explicitly. Let \(\lambda_{\min}c_1>3/8\), \(\eta_+=1-\lambda_{\max}c_2>0\), let \(B_c\) bound the constant offsets, and put \(\kappa_0=c_1\min_i a_i\), \(H=\lceil1/\kappa_0\rceil\). A sufficient arithmetic onset is
\[
1+\left\lceil\max\left\{174,\frac{B_c}{\eta_+},\kappa_0^{-2},
\frac{\max(H,B_H)}{\kappa_0}\right\}\right\rceil.
\]
This is not the analytic onset of the moment estimates.

There is a substantial implementation issue with the chosen high mean. The simplex inequality \cite[Corollary~6.4]{Polymath8b} gives
\[
\frac{\sum_iJ_i(F)}{I(F)}\le
\delta_s\frac{k}{k-1}\log k<\delta_s(\log k+1).
\]
Thus \(\delta_s\le10^{-5}\) and a mean exceeding \(999999\) require
\(\log k>99\,999\,899\,999\).
This is a design-specific dimension floor, not a theorem that every approach must have a huge onset. It shows why merely asking for the hidden constants of this implementation cannot justify overlap with a finite certificate of a few hundred digits. No finite certificate is assumed or replayed in this paper.

\paragraph{Provenance and limitations.}
The manuscript consolidates supplied AI-assisted research notes and new audit derivations. The attachment reports an independent model review and conditional formalization; neither the original referee output nor an executable Lean project was available for replay in this audit. No statement here claims human peer review, journal acceptance, formal verification of the analytic input, or worldwide priority. The accompanying finite checker verifies identities and rational margins, not the spectral estimate or an infinite tail theorem. The manuscript should be shared as a conditional research preprint unless and until the full actual-atom argument and this assembly receive specialist scrutiny. Authorship and affiliations are intentionally left unset in the source.

# Archive (6) review: elementary re-audit, actual source progress, and the unproved tail boundary

## 0. Disposition and evidence level

**Verdict: FORMAL SOURCE CONSTRUCTION ADVANCED; UNCONDITIONAL TAIL NOT ESTABLISHED BY THIS ARCHIVE.**

This is a review of the supplied `f3680730-21fd-4bc3-b8e9-fac9ae820a7d-aristotle (6).tar.gz`, together with the current conditional manuscript and FCHS-patched actual-atom supplement. It is not a replacement proof of every analytic theorem in the programme.

The archive contains 1,069 Lean files in total and 65 Lean files under `RequestProject/Erdos287/SourceChain/`. Those counts are inventory data, not proof strength. The source sets Lean/mathlib to v4.28.0. The archive reports successful builds; this review did NOT rerun them because Lean/lake is unavailable in the review environment. No source file in the input archive was changed.

The quoted latest response accurately describes a *top-layer re-audit*. It does not claim to prove the tail. More advanced physical-source work is already present elsewhere in the same archive; it must not be discarded or confused with the scope of that last response.

## 1. What the latest top-layer result really supplies

`ERDOS287_TOPLAYER_PACKAGE_REAUDIT.md` explicitly limits itself to `Defs`, `TopLayer`, `Cnum`, `Window`, `Counterexample`, `PrimeFree`, and `Blocker`. It states that no Lean source was modified.

Its algebraic and structural results are useful: top-layer congruences, small-cardinality obstructions, exact reciprocal-subset numerator maxima C(j), prime-power window exclusion, harmonic window constraints, eventual prime-freeness, and the contradiction from two adjacent blocked positions.

Independent exact rational enumeration in the companion checker reproduces

    C(1..9) = 1,3,11,25,137,137,1019,2143,7129

and the witness

    sum_{s in {1,2,3,4,5,7}} 1/s = 1019/420.

This is not an independent Lean rebuild and not a proof of any asymptotic prime supply. In particular, `Gap2CE.excludedPP_blockerPair` assumes the two excluded prime powers and their divisibility into adjacent positions. It does not construct those witnesses for every sufficiently large source.

## 2. Important progress that must be retained

The newer `ERDOS287_PARAMETER_SOURCEFIT_JUNCTION_REPORT.md` and the matching code go beyond the elementary report:

- `Physical/Factorization/ActualParams.lean`: an actual fixed scalar-parameter choice, the small-prime exponent bound, and `atom_factorization_actual` on `CritRegime`/`CritCell`.
- `Physical/TypeII/ProviderDictionary.lean`: exact `physCoefAtom_eq_dict`, one-boundedness, disjoint/coprime supports, and all three boxed kernel ranges, with epsilon = kappa/2000.
- `Physical/TypeII/SourceComposed.lean`: `scalarTypeII_eq_cells`, `packet_typeII_eq_cells`, and `physCell_contract`. The source is actually constructed. The designated pair is already part of the packet index; it must not be counted a second time.
- `SourceChain/W4Route.lean`: finite source-to-positive-square Cauchy, a generic fixed-A positive domination, the corrected FCHS expression, square-root exponent propagation, and packet arithmetic.
- `Physical/Tail.lean`: the exact physical remainder is connected to the existing conditional tail boundary.

Thus the earlier description “the physical source has not been defined at all” is stale. The remaining difficulty is instantiating and proving the analytic estimates and main-term framework for that actual source.

## 3. The canonical conclusion is already defined, but not proved without hypotheses

`CurrentTail/TailBoundary.lean:33-34` defines

    def Tail287Statement : Prop :=
      ∃ M0 : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℕ, ∀ hA : Erdos287Counterexample A,
        A.max' hA.nonempty < M0

This is the requested pre-effectivity target. No numerical M0 is required.

`Physical/Tail.lean:121-125` proves only

    Tail287_of_physical
      (Fw : OneSidedFrameworkFor F.R F.target)
      (hgood : eventually physical/sieve good)
      (hrel : IsLittleOTarget F.Rrel F.target)
      (hbase : IsLittleOTarget F.Rbase F.target) : Tail287Statement

All four inputs remain arguments. Moreover, F itself is an arbitrary `PhysicalFamily`; a final application needs one actually constructed family whose target is the intended normalization and whose coefficients, presieve and prime counts are the literal source.

The `OneSidedFrameworkFor` argument is substantial. It includes a scale selection, actual finite weights, a seven-block moment dictionary and simultaneous contact-window control for every sufficiently large exact word. Proving Cauchy's numerical consumer is not the same as constructing this framework.

The exact counterexample predicate in `ProblemStatement.lean` requires every denominator to exceed 1. The historical `Gap2CE` only requires positivity and admits `{1}`. The final theorem must use `Tail287Statement`/`Erdos287Counterexample`, not an unconditional nonexistence claim about the broader type.

## 4. Definitions of estimates are not estimates

`Physical/TypeII/RemainingProviders.lean` states at its beginning that its provider declarations are unproved analytic inputs. It defines:

- `PascadiCriticalCellProvider kappa`;
- `OrdinaryBVUremProvider kappa`;
- `SWSeq`.

`scalarTypeII_bound_of_providers` is proved *from arguments* of the first two types. The source identities preceding it are real theorems; the analytic providers are still assumptions.

Similarly, `W4Route.lean:160-175` defines `W4DiagEstimate`, `W4RamEstimate`, and `W4SpecEstimate`, and proves `W4_bound_of_pieces` from those three estimates plus a structural split. The latter theorem adds three already-assumed inequalities; it is not a proof of the spectral large sieve.

A static symbol search in the current `SourceChain/Physical` subtree found no direct invocation of `source_to_W4`, `CleanAtom`, `AstraAtomBound`, `W4SpecEstimate` or `W4_bound_of_pieces`. This limited search is not a semantic impossibility result; it is consistent with the archive's explicit provider boundary and shows why a generic W4 lemma must not be presented as an already-instantiated physical-source theorem.

Clean `#print axioms` output does not remove theorem binders. For example, `theorem conditional_example (P : Prop) (h : P) : P := h` introduces no new global axiom, yet it proves P only from h. Inspect full types as well as axiom dependencies. [L1,L2]

## 5. Interfaces to repair before trying to discharge the providers

### 5.1 Quantifier order and actual affine data

The current `PascadiCriticalCellProvider` chooses C and X0 before quantifying over every A, Bres and scalar parameter set. It also has no A>0, Bres != 0, or coprimality hypothesis on these affine coefficients. The supplied actual-atom paper fixes admissible affine A,B first and permits its constants to depend on them.

Therefore the supplied theorem cannot simply instantiate this provider as written. This review does not assert that every possible strengthened provider is false. It identifies a theorem-scope mismatch.

Repair by fixing the finite actual affine tuple, smooth profiles and scalar construction before choosing constants; prove a source-specific bound with the actual admissibility assumptions. Then take maxima over the finite pair/box family if justified. Do not prove a broader statement accidentally demanded by an abstraction, and do not add the needed source-specific estimate as an unproved final assumption.

### 5.2 The allowed base exponent is incompatible with the imported bound

The proved `physAtom_provider_contract` exports epsilon = kappa/2000. The provider currently allows f <= X^(kappa/1000), whereas the actual-atom supplement assumes sigma <= epsilon/100. Thus the formal base cap is 200 times the supplied sufficient cap.

Even the retained final packet margin becomes negative if one simply substitutes those displayed constants:

    epsilon/2 - (391/256)(kappa/1000) = -327 kappa / 256000.

One compatible conservative repair is

    epsilon = kappa/2000,
    sigma = kappa/1000000,
    delta_spectator = sigma/4.

Then sigma <= epsilon/100 and

    epsilon/2 - (391/256)sigma = 63609 kappa / 256000000 > 0.

The paired spectator lcm exponent 2 delta_spectator = sigma/2 leaves room for fixed slopes and the growing presieve. Its actual bound must still be proved. It is also permissible to derive and use a genuinely stronger exported epsilon, with proof. Merely quoting the old scalar margin is not sufficient.

Do not confuse the source cutoff parameter named K in `physCell` with the number of Maynard forms; the code uses K in several different roles.

### 5.3 Roughness and SW must belong to the actual source

The current critical provider assumes only dyadic support and `SWSeq`; it does not require the roughness hypotheses used by the published Type-II reduction or the cleaned atom. `SWSeq` also lacks the additional coprimality-mask parameter present in Maynard's stated SW condition. [M]

The current `OrdinaryBVUremProvider` quantifies over arbitrary bounded dyadic alpha,beta without ANY SW/distribution premise. Being below the one-half modulus level does not itself give an equidistribution theorem for arbitrary coefficients.

This is not presented as a verified counterexample to the entire existing `physUrem` proposition. The repair must either derive an estimate for the actual Heath--Brown sequences, including the precise relative-centering and coprimality condition used in its proof, or reformulate a sufficient provider with those hypotheses and then prove they hold. The last theorem must not retain a newly named unproved provider.

### 5.4 Product scale and norms

The formal provider currently assumes only N*M <= S.X. The actual-atom proof uses x=MN (up to explicit fixed comparability). Either restore that relation on the actual critical cells or separately prove the small-product ranges. Do not identify different scale variables without an inequality ledger.

A packetwise inverse-log estimate cannot be multiplied by a polynomial number of packets. Retain the relative-BDH density ordering; only fixed-power errors may use the crude packet count. Main-term normalization must be the actual positive N_X I, not a freely inflated `target` chosen to trivialize little-o.

## 6. The FCHS correction is in the code, but needs downstream propagation

`W4Route.lean:135-168` correctly defines the selected corrected expression with FCHS. The old expression is retained for regression only.

The published supplement now displays FCHS in (6.5), but its immediately following g-scaling prose and list of four monomials are unchanged. A display-only patch is not itself a proof that the old range calculation survives.

The companion `FCHS_AND_PARAMETER_REPAIR.md` supplies two elementary repairs:

1. If 0<=F<=B0 and 0<=H<=S, then

       F C H S <= B0 C S^2,

   hence the corrected square-root term is bounded by

       sqrt(F C^2 + 2 B0 C S^2).

   Use actual length envelopes to establish F <= C_* B0 with a fixed constant if the literal dyadic variables do not satisfy F <= B0 pointwise. This changes constants, not exponents.

2. With F=F0/g, C=C0/g,

       sqrt(F)*sqrt(F C^2+B0 C S^2+F C H S)
       = sqrt(F0)/g * sqrt(F0 C0^2/g^2+B0 C0 S^2+F0 C0 H S/g).

   Thus the claimed 1/g domination survives, with the formerly omitted last term recorded explicitly.

Primary-source caution: Pascadi's displayed proof has an intermediate FCHS/B term and a later simplified FHS term after prefactor cancellation. Do not describe those different expressions as the same formula. Retaining the archive's conservative enlarged FCHS expression is legitimate in ranges where the domination is justified, but it is not a verbatim transcription of every displayed stage. [P]

A documentation-only direction error also appears at `W4Route.lean:145-146`: the theorem below proves `old <= new`. A valid bound by the smaller old RHS would imply a weaker bound by the new RHS (under its positivity assumptions), not the reverse. Correct the comment, not the already-correct algebraic theorem.

None of these algebraic repairs proves the actual W4 spectral estimate.

## 7. What the next run must deliver

The correct unit of work is not another top-layer audit. It is:

    actual PhysicalFamily
      + proven correct provider instances
      + actual HB/partial-summation / noncritical / centering assembly
      + proven one-sided seven-block framework
      -> a closed term of Tail287Statement.

The next prompt fixes that objective, preserves already-constructed source data, and prevents escaping into a new generic interface.

For formal success, the final exported theorem must have no unresolved analytic or framework parameters and must be consumable by an independent file containing an `example : Tail287Statement := ...` outside sections with assumptions. A citation in a comment is not a Lean proof term. Missing deep formal results remain explicit provider dependencies even when the corresponding paper theorem is accepted informally.

For paper-level reconciliation, every remaining provider must have a complete stated written theorem, exact hypothesis match, and proof/citation chain. Standard library formalization incompleteness and a missing mathematical argument are distinct statuses. Neither an earlier model PASS nor this source review settles the latter.

## 8. Publication verdict

Keep the present main manuscript conditional until the actual analytic estimate AND its source/main-term integration have been verified at the claimed level. The archive does not justify promoting Hypothesis 9.1 to an unconditional theorem. A complete conditional Lean dependency certificate is useful, but is not an unconditional formal tail proof.

Effectivity/finite splice is separate. No additional finite endpoint is inferred here; the elementary prime-free threshold and arithmetic height lemmas do not prove all remaining finite cases.

# Algebraic FCHS propagation and compatible parameter choices

**Scope.** The statements proved here are elementary implications. They do not prove a spectral large-sieve estimate, a provider, the tail theorem, or a finite splice. No input Lean or PDF was modified. These additions should be integrated and checked in the next Aristotle run.

## A. Keep the corrected expression, and pay it

For nonnegative F,C,B0,S,H with F<=B0 and H<=S,

\[
FCHS\le B_0CS^2,
\]

because FH<=B0 S and CS>=0. Consequently,

\[
FC^2+B_0CS^2+FCHS\le FC^2+2B_0CS^2.
\]

Monotonicity of the square root yields the corresponding root bound. More generally, F<=c B0 and H<=d S give FCHS<=cd B0 C S^2 for nonnegative fixed c,d.

The source uses length envelopes Bbar~NR and Fbar~N/Q, with Q,R>=1. Therefore Fbar<=c Bbar for one fixed constant. With g>=1, F=Fbar/g remains within that envelope. If actual dyadic B0 is much smaller than its upper envelope, enlarge the nonnegative upper bound before applying the lemma; do not assert F<=B0 for every unmodified dyadic cell.

This makes the enlarged term no worse than a fixed multiple of an already-present square-root monomial. It explains how the four range comparisons can be retained without silently omitting the extra C.

## B. Correct g-scaling identity

Let g>0, F=F0/g, C=C0/g, and all radicands be nonnegative. Then

\[
\sqrt F\sqrt{FC^2+B_0CS^2+FCHS}
=
\frac{\sqrt{F_0}}g
\sqrt{\frac{F_0C_0^2}{g^2}+B_0C_0S^2+\frac{F_0C_0HS}{g}}.
\]

Proof: square both nonnegative sides and expand. Both equal

\[
\frac{F_0^2C_0^2}{g^4}
+\frac{F_0B_0C_0S^2}{g^2}
+\frac{F_0^2C_0HS}{g^3}.
\]

For g>=1, the right-hand side is bounded by the same expression with the two internal reciprocal-g factors replaced by 1, times 1/g. The exceptional factor involving C sqrt(F) also decreases with g.

## C. Do not confuse the primary paper's two stages

The normalized algebraic identity in Pascadi's proof is

\[
\frac{B_0}{C}
\sqrt{H^2S^4FC/B_0}
\sqrt{C^2(FC/B_0+S^2)+FCHS/B_0}
=
HS^2\sqrt F\sqrt{FC^2+B_0CS^2+FHS}
\]

for positive B0,C and nonnegative other data. Squaring verifies it directly. The intermediate FCHS/B0 is not the same normalization as the final FHS.

The archive deliberately uses a larger FCHS envelope at the final stage. Under C>=1 that enlargement is a valid inequality. The A/B lemmas above show a conservative way to pay it. At short scales not covered by C>=1, use the actual positive-scale theorem convention or a direct bound; do not infer the enlargement without hypotheses.

Correct the documentation comment at W4Route.lean:145-146: the proved order is `pascadiInnerOld <= pascadiInner`. A bound by the smaller RHS implies a bound by the larger one. The reverse implication does not follow. This concerns bound ordering, not the validity of an unproved old estimate.

## D. Explicit parameter repair at the current source contract

The source contract exports

\[
\epsilon=\kappa/2000.
\]

The current provider allows \(\sigma_{old}=\kappa/1000\), but the supplied actual-atom theorem only proves a sufficient range \(\sigma\le\epsilon/100\). With the displayed packet exponent,

\[
\frac\epsilon2-\frac{391}{256}\sigma_{old}
=-\frac{327}{256000}\kappa<0.
\]

A consistent conservative replacement is

\[
\sigma=\kappa/1000000,
\qquad
\delta_{spectator}=\sigma/4.
\]

Then

\[
\sigma<\epsilon/100,
\qquad
2\delta_{spectator}=\sigma/2<\sigma,
\]

and

\[
\boxed{
\frac\epsilon2-\frac{391}{256}\sigma
=\frac{63609}{256000000}\kappa>0.
}
\]

The remaining exponent half is available for fixed slopes, the actual growing presieve and cutoff constants. That support statement must be proved from the constructed physical family. This repair narrows a sufficient source class; it is not a theorem that the broader old provider was false. A proved stronger epsilon export is an alternative.

Order of choices: choose positive kappa and the fixed scalar construction; choose the spectral reserve and support exponents; construct the fixed Maynard dimension/test function and affine tuple; then let the physical scale tend to infinity. Track any exponent dependence on dimension rather than hiding it in an absolute constant.

## E. Finite checks

`verify_review.py` verifies these polynomial/rational implications on exact finite fixtures and the numerical fraction identities. The proofs are the algebra above; the fixtures are regression checks, not substitutes for universal reasoning or analytic estimates.

  30: /-! ## The excluded-prime-power predicate -/
  31: 
  32: /-- `ExcludedPP M q` : `q` is a prime power `p^e` (`e ≥ 1`) such that the largest
  33: reciprocal-sum numerator over subsets of `{1,…,⌊M/q⌋}` is `< p`.  By
  34: `primePower_window_exclusion`, no element of a reciprocal-sum-`1` set `A ⊆ [1,M]` is
  35: divisible by `q`. -/
  36: def ExcludedPP (M q : ℕ) : Prop :=
  37:   ∃ p e : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ 1 ≤ e ∧ q = p ^ e ∧ C (M / q) < (p : ℤ)
  38: 
  39: /-
  40: A prime power `r^e` is excluded whenever the window numerator bound at some
  41: `j ≥ ⌊M/r^e⌋` is below the base `r`.
  42: -/
  43: theorem excludedPP_of_le {M r e j : ℕ} (hr : r.Prime) (he : 1 ≤ e)
  44:     (hj : M / r ^ e ≤ j) (hC : C j < (r : ℤ)) : ExcludedPP M (r ^ e) := by
  45:   exact ⟨ r, e, hr, he, rfl, lt_of_le_of_lt ( C_mono hj ) hC ⟩
  46: 
  47: /-
  48: A prime `p` with `M/2 < p ≤ M` is excluded (`q = p`, window `⌊M/p⌋ = 1`,
  49: `C 1 = 1 < p`).
  50: -/
  51: theorem excludedPP_self_of_large {M p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpM : p ≤ M)
  52:     (hM2 : M < 2 * p) : ExcludedPP M p := by
  53:   use p, 1;
  54:   exact ⟨ hp, by norm_num, by norm_num, by rw [ show M / p = 1 by exact Nat.le_antisymm ( Nat.le_of_lt_succ <| Nat.div_lt_of_lt_mul <| by linarith ) ( Nat.div_pos hpM hp.pos ) ] ; exact by have := Erdos287.C_one; norm_num at *; linarith [ hp.two_le ] ⟩
  55: 
  56: /-
  57: **Excluded prime powers are never denominators.**  If `ExcludedPP M q` and
  58: `q ∣ x`, then `x` cannot belong to a reciprocal-sum-`1` set `A ⊆ [1,M]`.
  59: -/
  60: theorem ExcludedPP.not_dvd_mem {M q : ℕ} (hq : ExcludedPP M q)
  61:     {A : Finset ℕ} (hpos : ∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a) (hAM : ∀ a ∈ A, a ≤ M)
  62:     (hsum : ∑ a ∈ A, (1 : ℚ) / a = 1) {x : ℕ} (hxA : x ∈ A) (hqx : q ∣ x) : False := by
  63:   obtain ⟨ p, e, hp, he, rfl, hpC ⟩ := hq;
  64:   apply primePower_window_exclusion A M p e hp hpos hAM hsum he (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_of_dvd (hpos x hxA) hqx) (hAM x hxA)) hpC x hxA hqx
  65: 
  66: /-! ## Specialization to a gap-`≤2` counterexample -/
  67: 
  68: namespace Gap2CE
  69: 
  70: variable (ce : Gap2CE)
  71: 
  72: /-
  73: An excluded prime-power multiple is a hole of the counterexample.
  74: -/
  75: theorem notMem_of_excludedPP {q x : ℕ} (hq : ExcludedPP ce.M q) (hqx : q ∣ x) :
  76:     x ∉ ce.A := by
  77:   exact fun hx => ExcludedPP.not_dvd_mem hq ce.hpos (fun a ha => Finset.le_max' _ _ ha) ce.hsum hx hqx
  78: 
  79: /-
  80: **Reusable blocker pair.**  If `x, x+1 ∈ [N, M]`, `q₁` and `q₂` are excluded
  81: prime powers with `q₁ ∣ x` and `q₂ ∣ x+1`, then no `Gap2CE` exists.
  82: -/
  83: theorem excludedPP_blockerPair {x q₁ q₂ : ℕ}
  84:     (hx0 : ce.N ≤ x) (hx1 : x + 1 ≤ ce.M)
  85:     (hq1 : ExcludedPP ce.M q₁) (hq2 : ExcludedPP ce.M q₂)
  86:     (hd1 : q₁ ∣ x) (hd2 : q₂ ∣ x + 1) : False := by
  87:   exact ce.blockerPair_contradiction hx0 hx1 ( ce.notMem_of_excludedPP hq1 ( by simpa using hd1 ) ) ( ce.notMem_of_excludedPP hq2 ( by simpa using hd2 ) )
  88:

  94: theorem forced_right {n : ℕ} (hn0 : ce.N ≤ n) (hn1 : n + 1 ≤ ce.M)
  95:     (hhole : n ∉ ce.A) : n + 1 ∈ ce.A := by

  99: A hole at `n+1` inside `[N, M]` forces its left neighbour `n` into `A`.
 100: -/
 101: theorem forced_left {n : ℕ} (hn0 : ce.N ≤ n) (hn1 : n + 1 ≤ ce.M)
 102:     (hhole : n + 1 ∉ ce.A) : n ∈ ce.A := by

Lines 4–68:

```text
   4: # Erdős Problem #287 — the exact problem statement
   5: 
   6: The published problem asks: for every finite strictly increasing sequence of integers
   7: 
   8:   `1 < n₁ < n₂ < ⋯ < n_k`  with  `∑ 1/nᵢ = 1`,
   9: 
  10: is some consecutive gap `n_{i+1} - n_i` at least `3`?
  11: 
  12: This file introduces the **exact** project-local predicate `Erdos287Counterexample A`
  13: describing a hypothetical counterexample and relates it to the broader historical
  14: compiler type `Gap2CE`:
  15: 
  16: * `Erdos287Counterexample` requires `2 ≤ A.card`, `1 < a` for every `a ∈ A`,
  17:   `∑_{a ∈ A} 1/a = 1` and all consecutive gaps `≤ 2`;
  18: * `Gap2CE` only requires positivity (`0 < a`), so it admits irrelevant objects such as
  19:   `A = {1}` (`gap2CE_one`, banked below as an explicit witness).  The two types are
  20:   therefore **not** equivalent; the bridge goes one way only
  21:   (`Erdos287Counterexample.toGap2CE`), which is the direction the reduction needs.
  22: 
  23: We also give the ordered-sequence formulation (`erdos287_seq_of_no_counterexample`),
  24: literally matching the public statement.
  25: -/
  26: 
  27: open scoped BigOperators
  28: 
  29: namespace Erdos287
  30: 
  31: /-- **The exact Erdős #287 counterexample predicate.**  A finite set `A` of integers `> 1`
  32: whose reciprocals sum to `1`, with at least two elements, in which every non-maximal
  33: element is followed within distance `2` (i.e. every consecutive gap of the sorted list of
  34: `A` is at most `2`). -/
  35: structure Erdos287Counterexample (A : Finset ℕ) : Prop where
  36:   /-- At least two denominators. -/
  37:   card_ge : 2 ≤ A.card
  38:   /-- Every denominator exceeds `1`. -/
  39:   one_lt : ∀ a ∈ A, 1 < a
  40:   /-- The reciprocals sum to `1`. -/
  41:   sum_one : ∑ a ∈ A, (1 : ℚ) / a = 1
  42:   /-- Every non-maximal element is followed within distance `2`. -/
  43:   gap_le_two : ∀ a ∈ A, (∃ b ∈ A, a < b) → (a + 1 ∈ A ∨ a + 2 ∈ A)
  44: 
  45: namespace Erdos287Counterexample
  46: 
  47: variable {A : Finset ℕ} (h : Erdos287Counterexample A)
  48: 
  49: include h
  50: 
  51: /-- The underlying set is nonempty. -/
  52: theorem nonempty : A.Nonempty := Finset.card_pos.1 (by have := h.card_ge; omega)
  53: 
  54: /-- **Bridge to the historical compiler type.**  Every exact counterexample is in
  55: particular a `Gap2CE`. -/
  56: def toGap2CE : Gap2CE where
  57:   A := A
  58:   hne := h.nonempty
  59:   hpos := fun a ha => lt_trans Nat.zero_lt_one (h.one_lt a ha)
  60:   hsum := h.sum_one
  61:   hgap := by
  62:     intro a ha hne
  63:     refine h.gap_le_two a ha ⟨A.max' h.nonempty, Finset.max'_mem _ _, ?_⟩
  64:     exact lt_of_le_of_ne (Finset.le_max' _ _ ha) hne
  65: 
  66: @[simp] theorem toGap2CE_A : (h.toGap2CE).A = A := rfl
  67: 
  68: @[simp] theorem toGap2CE_M : (h.toGap2CE).M = A.max' h.nonempty := rfl
```

Lines 104–150:

```text
 104: /-! ## Non-vacuity guards
 105: 
 106: The predicate is not accidentally unsatisfiable for trivial reasons: each family of fields
 107: is separately realisable, and it is only their *conjunction* that is at stake. -/
 108: 
 109: /-- `{2,3,4}` satisfies every field except the reciprocal-sum one (its sum is `13/12`). -/
 110: theorem sanity_gap_fields_satisfiable :
 111:     2 ≤ ({2, 3, 4} : Finset ℕ).card ∧ (∀ a ∈ ({2, 3, 4} : Finset ℕ), 1 < a) ∧
 112:       (∀ a ∈ ({2, 3, 4} : Finset ℕ), (∃ b ∈ ({2, 3, 4} : Finset ℕ), a < b) →
 113:         (a + 1 ∈ ({2, 3, 4} : Finset ℕ) ∨ a + 2 ∈ ({2, 3, 4} : Finset ℕ))) ∧
 114:       ∑ a ∈ ({2, 3, 4} : Finset ℕ), (1 : ℚ) / a = 13 / 12 := by
 115:   refine ⟨by decide, by decide, by decide, ?_⟩
 116:   norm_num
 117: 
 118: /-- `{2,3,6}` satisfies every field except the gap one (`3` and `6` are `3` apart). -/
 119: theorem sanity_sum_field_satisfiable :
 120:     2 ≤ ({2, 3, 6} : Finset ℕ).card ∧ (∀ a ∈ ({2, 3, 6} : Finset ℕ), 1 < a) ∧
 121:       ∑ a ∈ ({2, 3, 6} : Finset ℕ), (1 : ℚ) / a = 1 ∧
 122:       ¬ (∀ a ∈ ({2, 3, 6} : Finset ℕ), (∃ b ∈ ({2, 3, 6} : Finset ℕ), a < b) →
 123:         (a + 1 ∈ ({2, 3, 6} : Finset ℕ) ∨ a + 2 ∈ ({2, 3, 6} : Finset ℕ))) := by
 124:   refine ⟨by decide, by decide, ?_, by decide⟩
 125:   norm_num
 126: 
 127: 
 128: /-- The historical type `Gap2CE` is genuinely broader: `A = {1}` inhabits it.  (This is why
 129: the reduction is phrased against `Erdos287Counterexample` and only *maps into* `Gap2CE`.) -/
 130: def gap2CE_one : Gap2CE where
 131:   A := {1}
 132:   hne := ⟨1, by simp⟩
 133:   hpos := by intro a ha; simp at ha; omega
 134:   hsum := by simp
 135:   hgap := by
 136:     intro a ha hne
 137:     simp at ha
 138:     exact absurd (by simp [ha]) hne
 139: 
 140: /-- ... and it is not an exact counterexample. -/
 141: theorem not_erdos287Counterexample_one : ¬ Erdos287Counterexample {1} := by
 142:   intro h
 143:   have := h.one_lt 1 (by simp)
 144:   omega
 145: 
 146: /-! ## The ordered-sequence formulation -/
 147: 
 148: /-- **Public statement, ordered form.**  If no finite set is an `Erdos287Counterexample`,
 149: then every finite strictly increasing sequence `1 < n 0 < n 1 < ⋯ < n (k-1)` whose
 150: reciprocals sum to `1` has a consecutive gap of at least `3`. -/
```

  39: noncomputable def beta (S : ScalarParams) : ℝ :=

  76: theorem critRegime_Tchoice {κ X : ℝ} (hκ : 0 < κ) (hκ' : κ < 1 / 100000) (hX : 1 < X) :

 168: /-- **Provider contract of every admissible sector of an actual critical cell.**
 169: With `Q = N X^{-κ}`, `S = E₁`, `R = E₂` (box-endpoint products of colours 1 and 2),
 170: the three one-bounded factor sequences have the stated supports, pairwise coprime supports,
 171: the sign/weight scalar is bounded by `|Γ| w`, and the three boxed range conditions hold
 172: with `ε = κ/2000`. -/
 173: theorem physAtom_provider_contract {κ N : ℝ} (h : CritRegime S κ) (hN : CritCell S κ N)
 174:     (Γ : ℝ) {J : ℕ} {P : Fin J → Fin S.H} (hP : S.BoxAdm J P) (χ : Fin S.Kc → Fin 3) :
 175:     let c := S.atomColour κ N J P
 176:     let Q := N * S.X ^ (-κ)
 177:     let Sb := cprod (S.boxVec J P) c 1 J
 178:     let R := cprod (S.boxVec J P) c 2 J
 179:     -- one-boundedness
 180:     (∀ n, |S.lowFactor J P c χ n| ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ n, |S.colFactor J P c χ 1 n| ≤ 1) ∧
 181:       (∀ n, |S.colFactor J P c χ 2 n| ≤ 1) ∧
 182:     -- supports
 183:       (∀ n, S.lowFactor J P c χ n ≠ 0 → (n : ℝ) ≤ Q) ∧
 184:       (∀ n, S.colFactor J P c χ 1 n ≠ 0 → (n : ℝ) ≤ Sb) ∧
 185:       (∀ n, S.colFactor J P c χ 2 n ≠ 0 → (n : ℝ) ≤ R) ∧
 186:     -- coprime supports
 187:       (∀ a s, S.lowFactor J P c χ a ≠ 0 → S.colFactor J P c χ 1 s ≠ 0 → Nat.Coprime a s) ∧
 188:       (∀ a t, S.lowFactor J P c χ a ≠ 0 → S.colFactor J P c χ 2 t ≠ 0 → Nat.Coprime a t) ∧
 189:       (∀ s t, S.colFactor J P c χ 1 s ≠ 0 → S.colFactor J P c χ 2 t ≠ 0 → Nat.Coprime s t) ∧
 190:     -- scalar
 191:       |Γ * ((-1 : ℝ) ^ J * S.atomWeight J P c)| ≤ |Γ| * S.atomWeight J P c ∧
 192:     -- boxed range conditions
 193:       N ^ 2 * R ^ 2 * Sb ≤ S.X ^ (1 - 8 * (κ / 2000)) ∧
 194:       N ^ ((71 : ℝ) / 50) * R * Sb ^ ((93 : ℝ) / 50) ≤ S.X ^ (1 - 16 * (κ / 2000)) ∧
 195:       N ^ ((39 : ℝ) / 25) * Q ^ ((11 : ℝ) / 25) * R ^ 2 * Sb ^ 5 ≤
 196:         S.X ^ (2 - 32 * (κ / 2000)) := by

   3: /-!
   4: # Erdős #287 — remaining analytic providers for the actual Type-II source
   5: 
   6: **ERDŐS #287 REMAINS OPEN.  TAIL-287 IS NOT BANKED.  Nothing in this file is proved about
   7: primes: every `def … : Prop` below is an UNPROVED analytic input, stated in full.**
   8: 
   9: The source side is closed by `scalarTypeII_eq_cells` / `physCell_contract`.  What remains for
  10: the *critical* Type-II part of the actual source is:
  11: 
  12: * `PascadiCriticalCellProvider κ` — **Pascadi's beyond-half estimate** for the actual critical
  13:   cells.  The moduli `l r` reach `D_tot = X^{59/100} > X^{1/2}`, so ordinary BV/BDH does **not**
  14:   supply it.
  15: * `OrdinaryBVUremProvider κ` — the `h_l U_r` part: only the modulus `f l` with
  16:   `l ≤ N X^{-κ} ≤ X^{1/3}` carries a congruence, so this is an **ordinary** BV/BDH-range input
  17:   (level below `1/2`).
  18: * `SWSeq` — the Siegel–Walfisz condition on the smooth-variable sequence `α`, used as a
  19:   hypothesis inside `PascadiCriticalCellProvider` (as in every Bombieri–Vinogradov-type
  20:   bilinear estimate).
  21: 
  22: `scalarTypeII_bound_of_cells` is the kernel-proved composition: per-atom cell bounds plus a bound
  23: on `physUrem` give a bound on the scalar Type-II source, with the atom total variation
  24: `∑_{J ≤ T²} H^J 3^J` (independent of `X`).  `scalarTypeII_bound_of_providers` instantiates it
  25: with the two providers.
  26: -/
  27: 
  28: open Finset Real
  29: 
  30: set_option autoImplicit false
  31: 
  32: namespace Erdos287.Physical.TypeII
  33: 
  34: open Erdos287.Physical.Sieve Erdos287.Physical.Sieve.ScalarParams Erdos287.Physical.Factor
  35: 
  36: open Classical in
  37: /-- Siegel–Walfisz condition for a sequence supported on `[N, 2N)`, moduli `q ≤ (log N)^B`. -/
  38: def SWSeq (α : ArithmeticFunction ℝ) (Nn : ℕ) (Aexp B C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  39:   ∀ q a : ℕ, 0 < q → (q : ℝ) ≤ Real.log Nn ^ B → Nat.Coprime a q →
  40:     |∑ n ∈ range (2 * Nn), (if n ≡ a [MOD q] then α n else 0) -
  41:       (1 / (Nat.totient q : ℝ)) * ∑ n ∈ range (2 * Nn), (if Nat.Coprime n q then α n else 0)|
  42:       ≤ C * Nn / Real.log Nn ^ Aexp
  43: 
  44: /-- **(UNPROVED) Pascadi's beyond-half estimate, at the actual critical Type-II cells.**
  45: For every saving exponent `A` and every Siegel–Walfisz constant `C_SW` there are a
  46: Siegel–Walfisz strength `A'`, a modulus range `(log N)^B`, and `C, X₀` such that for every scalar parameter set in the
  47: small-`ε₀` regime of `κ`, every critical cell `N_n`, `N_n M ≤ X`, every packet modulus
  48: `f ≤ X^{κ/1000}` with `(c, f) = 1`, every sequence pair `α ∼ N_n`, `β ∼ M` with `|α| ≤ B_α`,
  49: `|β| ≤ B_β` and `α` Siegel–Walfisz, and every admissible sector `(J, P)` and colouring `χ`,
  50: the dyadically summed cells of the atom are bounded by
  51: `C B_α B_β |Γ| w_{J,P} X / (f (log X)^A)`. -/
  52: def PascadiCriticalCellProvider (κ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  53:   ∀ Aexp Csw : ℝ, ∃ A' B C X0 : ℝ, ∀ S : ScalarParams, CritRegime S κ → X0 ≤ S.X →

 181:       have : 0 ≤ Bα * Bβ * |Γ| * S.atomWeight J P (S.atomColour κ Nn J P) := by positivity
 182:       nlinarith
 183:     calc C1 * Bα * Bβ * |Γ| * S.atomWeight J P (S.atomColour κ Nn J P) *
 184:           (S.X / (f * Real.log S.X ^ Aexp))
 185:         ≤ |Γ| * S.atomWeight J P (S.atomColour κ Nn J P) * (|C1| * Bα * Bβ) *
 186:           (S.X / (f * Real.log S.X ^ Aexp)) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right this hq
 187:       _ = _ := by ring
 188:   · exact h2 S hreg hX2 Nn M hN hNM Γ f c A Bres K K' hf0 hf hcf α β Bα Bβ hαb hβb hα hβ

  42: theorem source_to_W4 {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β] (Ω : Finset α) (π : α → β) (a : α → ℂ)
  43:     (G : β → ℂ) (m : ℕ) (ha : ∀ ω ∈ Ω, ‖a ω‖ ≤ 1)
  44:     (hm : ∀ b, (Ω.filter (fun ω => π ω = b)).card ≤ m) :
  45:     ‖∑ ω ∈ Ω, a ω * G (π ω)‖ ^ 2 ≤ Ω.card * (m * ∑ b ∈ Ω.image π, ‖G b‖ ^ 2) := by
  46:   have h1 : ‖∑ ω ∈ Ω, a ω * G (π ω)‖ ≤ ∑ ω ∈ Ω, ‖G (π ω)‖ := by
  47:     refine (norm_sum_le _ _).trans (Finset.sum_le_sum (fun ω hω => ?_))
  48:     rw [norm_mul]
  49:     exact mul_le_of_le_one_left (norm_nonneg _) (ha ω hω)
  50:   have h2 : (∑ ω ∈ Ω, ‖G (π ω)‖) ^ 2 ≤ Ω.card * ∑ ω ∈ Ω, ‖G (π ω)‖ ^ 2 :=
  51:     sq_sum_le_card_mul_sum_sq
  52:   have h3 : ∑ ω ∈ Ω, ‖G (π ω)‖ ^ 2 ≤ m * ∑ b ∈ Ω.image π, ‖G b‖ ^ 2 := by
  53:     rw [Finset.sum_comp (fun b => ‖G b‖ ^ 2) π, Finset.mul_sum]
  54:     refine Finset.sum_le_sum (fun b _ => ?_)
  55:     rw [nsmul_eq_mul]
  56:     exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (by exact_mod_cast hm b) (sq_nonneg _)
  57:   calc ‖∑ ω ∈ Ω, a ω * G (π ω)‖ ^ 2 ≤ (∑ ω ∈ Ω, ‖G (π ω)‖) ^ 2 :=
  58:         pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) h1 2
  59:     _ ≤ _ := h2
  60:     _ ≤ _ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h3 (Nat.cast_nonneg _)

  77: /-- **Fixed-`A` positive domination** `W_{A₀}(B₀,C₀,F₀) ≤ W₁(A₀B₀,C₀,F₀)`: an injective
  78: positive-stage map `ι` (e.g. `b ↦ A₀ b`) with `w ≤ w₁ ∘ ι`, `inner = inner₁ ∘ ι` and
  79: `ι(T) ⊆ T₁` gives domination, provided the target weights are non-negative.  It concerns the
  80: already-formed positive square only. -/
  81: theorem fixedA_domination {β γ : Type*} [DecidableEq γ] (T : Finset β) (T1 : Finset γ)
  82:     (ι : β → γ) (hinj : Set.InjOn ι T) (hsub : T.image ι ⊆ T1) (w : β → ℝ) (w1 : γ → ℝ)
  83:     (inner : β → ℂ) (inner1 : γ → ℂ) (hw : ∀ b ∈ T, w b ≤ w1 (ι b))
  84:     (hw1 : ∀ g ∈ T1, 0 ≤ w1 g) (hin : ∀ b ∈ T, inner b = inner1 (ι b)) :
  85:     W4 T w inner ≤ W4 T1 w1 inner1 := by
  86:   unfold W4
  87:   calc ∑ b ∈ T, w b * ‖inner b‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∑ b ∈ T, w1 (ι b) * ‖inner1 (ι b)‖ ^ 2 :=
  88:         Finset.sum_le_sum (fun b hb => by
  89:           rw [hin b hb]; exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hw b hb) (sq_nonneg _))
  90:     _ = ∑ g ∈ T.image ι, w1 g * ‖inner1 g‖ ^ 2 := (Finset.sum_image (f := fun g => w1 g * ‖inner1 g‖ ^ 2) hinj).symm
  91:     _ ≤ ∑ g ∈ T1, w1 g * ‖inner1 g‖ ^ 2 :=
  92:         Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg hsub (fun g hg _ =>
  93:           mul_nonneg (hw1 g hg) (sq_nonneg _))

 136: def pascadiInner (F C B0 S H : ℝ) : ℝ := F * C ^ 2 + B0 * C * S ^ 2 + F * C * H * S
