## 2. Principal theorems

### §18 `FiniteRepresentationModel`
Uses the project's exact type `Erdos287Counterexample A` (integers `> 1`, reciprocal sum 1,
consecutive gaps `≤ 2`, endpoint `M = max A`) — no change of convention.
`NoCounterexampleAt M`, `NoCounterexampleUpTo U`, `noCounterexampleUpTo_iff_finiteVerified`
(= V9 `FiniteVerifiedThrough`), `noCounterexample_all_iff` (`∀ M, NoCounterexampleAt M` is exactly
the full statement), `NoCounterexampleUpTo.mono`, `noCounterexampleUpTo_4e9`.

### §19 `PrimeLayer`
`L J = lcm(1..J)`, `A J = ∑_{j ≤ J} L J / j`.  **`primeLayer_exclusion`**: if `r` is prime,
`max A < (J+1) r` and `A J < r`, no element of a counterexample is divisible by `r` (proved in the
rational model via `r`-adic valuation, following the requested skeleton: `r_multiples`,
`coprime_L`, `num_le_A`, `C_le_A`).  Values: `L_2 = 2`, `A_2 = 3`, `L_5 = 60`, `A_5 = 137`,
`L_10 = 2520`, `A_10 = 7381` (kernel `decide`).

### §20 `HarmonicTwoHole`
`eta = 685/252`; **`eta_lt_exp`** (`685/252 < exp 1`, from Mathlib's `Real.exp_one_gt_d9`),
`log_eta_lt_one`, `harmonic_tail_le_log` (`∑_{n=H+1}^{M} 1/n ≤ log(M/H)`), `etaFloor`,
**`cannot_cross_two_holes`**, **`two_hole_exclusion`** (adjacent forbidden `h, h+1`,
`h ≤ M ≤ ⌊η (h+1)⌋` ⇒ contradiction), **`interval_exclusion_of_adjacent_holes`** (generic interval
theorem).  The literal log argument is used; the final interval theorem is not weakened.

### §21 `AdjacentPrimeLayer`
**`familyA_interval`** (`p = 2q+1`, both prime, `q > 137`: every `M ∈ [p−1, ⌊(685/252)p⌋]` is
excluded; hole `p−1 = 2q` via the `q`-layer with `J = 5` (`A 5 = 137 < q`, `M < 6q`), hole `p` via
the `p`-layer with `J = 2`), **`familyB_interval`**
(`p = 4q+1`, `q > 7381`; `J = 10` for `q`, `J = 2` for `p`), **`familyB_outside_goodPrimeHalf`**
(for `q > 3`: `(p−1)/2 = 2q` is composite and `3 ∣ (p+1)/2 = 2q+1 > 3`), `familyA_instance`.

### §23 `PrimeCertificates`
Mathlib has Lucas/Pocklington-style results only for specific forms and no ready witness checker,
so generic soundness lemmas were proved directly:
**`proth_sound`** (`q = u·2ⁿ+1`, `0 < u < 2ⁿ`, `a^((q−1)/2) ≡ −1 (mod q)` ⇒ `q` prime; `u` odd is
not needed), **`pocklington_sound`** (`q` prime, `p = c q + 1`, `c ≥ 1` (covers `c ∈ {2,4}`),
`p < q²`, `b^(p−1) ≡ 1`, `gcd(b^c − 1, p) = 1` ⇒ `p` prime), Boolean checkers `prothCheck`,
`pocklingtonCheck` with `prothCheck_sound`, `pocklingtonCheck_sound` (binary modular exponentiation
`Pratt.powMod` from the project's Pratt engine, proved correct, evaluated by the kernel; the Proth
checker also enforces `u` odd as part of the format), fixtures `prime_13/97/173/347`,
`malformed_proth_rejected`, `malformed_pocklington_rejected`, `familyA_from_certificates`.
No `native_decide`, no `bv_decide`, no probable-prime routine, no primality axiom.

# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V21 report: normalized sieve monotonicity and quadratic domination

**Erdős #287 remains OPEN.** V21 is finite algebra only. It proves no analytic statement and
claims no independence of actual primes (only independence of the finite CRT coordinates of the
principal model).

Namespace `Erdos287.ResearchBankV21`. Aggregator `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV21.lean`.
Append-only: no V2–V20 file, no earlier report and `ARISTOTLE_SUMMARY.md` were modified.

Status labels used (exactly): **LEAN BANK**, **LEAN CONDITIONAL**, **EXTERNAL PROVIDER**,
**FINITE REGRESSION**, **REPAIRED / RETIRED**, **OPEN**.

## Files

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `ResearchBankV21/FiniteSieveSetup.lean` | finite prime-subset model: `divSum` (`a_λ(S) = Σ_{A⊆S} λ(A)`), `numer`, `denom`, `normCost` (`C_λ(q)`), `odds` (`q/(1-q)`), `sum_supset_prod` |
| `ResearchBankV21/NormalizedSieveMonotonicity.lean` | exact identity and monotonicity; signed-coefficient firewalls |
| `ResearchBankV21/SpectatorStates.lean` | spectator states `Y_p`, repaired local law, conditional density, envelope `h(p) = 1/(p-K+1)` |
| `ResearchBankV21/ConditionalDensity.lean` | the repaired law derived by counting residues mod `p` |
| `ResearchBankV21/QuadraticDomination.lean` | finite product model, conditional expectation, **quadratic domination** |
| `ResearchBankV21/DensityCounterfixture.lean` | mod-11 counterfixture (`4/37 ≠ 1/10`) |
| `ResearchBankV21/Ledger.lean` | `v21Ledger = v20Ledger ++ v21New`, `v21_final_status` |
| `ResearchBankV21/AxiomAudit.lean` | `#print axioms` for all 43 V21 theorems |

## Principal theorems (all LEAN BANK)

- `NormalizedSieveMonotonicity.normCost_eq_sum_divSum` — for `0 ≤ q_p < 1`,
  `C_λ(q) = (Σ_A λ(A) ∏_{p∈A} q_p) / ∏_p (1-q_p) = Σ_S a_λ(S) ∏_{p∈S} q_p/(1-q_p)`
  (finite combinatorial expansion, no probability).
- `NormalizedSieveMonotonicity.normCost_mono` — if `a_λ(S) ≥ 0` for every `S` (NOT `λ(A) ≥ 0`)
  and `0 ≤ q_p ≤ h_p < 1`, then `C_λ(q) ≤ C_λ(h)`. The hypothesis used is the divisor-sum
  nonnegativity.
- `SpectatorStates`: `stateProb_sum_one` (`P(Y=k) = 1/(p-1)`, `P(Y=0) = (p-r-1)/(p-1)`),
  `condDensity_le_envelope` (`q_p(Y) ≤ h(p) = 1/(p-r-1) = 1/(p-K+1)`, `r = K-2`), `envelope_eq`,
  `average_condDensity`, `envelope_gt_raw`.
- `ConditionalDensity.repaired_law_from_residues` — the repaired law read off from the residues.
- `QuadraticDomination.quadratic_domination` — for every spectator-state law `μ ≥ 0`, every
  conditional density `q(y) ≤ h`, every complex amplitude `B` of the spectator states:

      E[|B|² S_λ(L_j)] ≤ C_λ(h) · E[|B|² 1_sifted],

  obtained from the conditional identity `condExp_eq_normCost_mul`
  (`E[S_λ | Y] = C_λ(q(Y)) · P(sifted | Y)`) and monotonicity. `quadratic_domination_signed_tensor`
  states it for `B = Σ_e c_e φ_e` (signs inside `B` before squaring); `quadratic_domination_spectator`
  for the repaired spectator law.

## Firewalls / regressions

- **REPAIRED / RETIRED** — V17-style inference "spectator-square weighting keeps the local density
  `1/(p-1)`". Counterfixture `DensityCounterfixture.spectator_square_density_not_invariant`
  (FINITE REGRESSION): mod 11, `L_i = t+1`, `L_j = 2t+1`, `L_k = 3t+1` on `L_i ≠ 0`,
  `W = (1 - ½·1_{L_k=0})²`; weighted density of `L_j = 0` is exactly `4/37`, raw density `1/10`,
  `4/37 ≠ 1/10`. `counterfixture_within_envelope` checks the repaired envelope still dominates.
- `signed_coefficient_nonneg_divSum` (FINITE REGRESSION) — `λ({p}) = -1 < 0` while every divisor
  sum is `≥ 0`; `monotonicity_needs_divSum_nonneg` — with a negative divisor sum monotonicity fails.

## Ledger

`Ledger.v21_final_status`: normalized sieve monotonicity — LEAN BANK; spectator-conditioned quadratic
domination — LEAN BANK; V17 density-invariance shortcut — REPAIRED / RETIRED; mod-11 counterfixture —
FINITE REGRESSION; independence of actual primes — OPEN; Erdős #287 — OPEN.

  with `π = ∏_j k_j!/(k_{j1}!k_{j2}!k_{j3}!) · 3^{-k_j}`; the expectation is a finite average of
  total mass one (`colouring_mass_one`); `piProb_inv_le`: `π^{-1} ≤ 3^R`. `G_zero_or_one`,

**Erdős #287 remains OPEN.** V23 reconnects the positive square to the original full-lcm principal
term. The finite CRT algebra, the signed expansion, the same-weight bound, the Euler-factor algebra,
the singular cancellation and the rational budget are kernel-proved; the Euler/Mellin asymptotic
and the hat-reference approximation are EXTERNAL PROVIDER interfaces.

## Principal theorems

### LEAN BANK
- `PrincipalCRTMeasure.principal_prob` — for an actual compatible CRT residue `t0`,
  `Prob_i(t ≡ t0 mod L0) = φ(A_i W0)/φ(A_i L0) · 1(gcd(A_i t0 + 1, A_i L0) = 1)`;
  `principal_Li_identity` — `Li/φ(A_i W0) · Prob = Li/φ(A_i L0) · (unit indicator)`.
  `FullLCMPrincipal.principal_prob_fullLCM` / `principal_sum_fullLCM` at the complete modulus
  `L0 = lcm(W0, s, q₁, …, q_r)`. The finite auxiliary set used for CRT probabilities is a model
  device; it is never passed to the prime-distribution theorem as a new modulus.
- `SameWeightPrincipal.signed_expansion` — `E[|B|² S_λ(L_j)]` with `B = Σ_e c_e φ_e` equals the
  original signed expression `Σ_d λ(d) Σ_{e,e'} c_e c̄_{e'} E[φ_e φ̄_{e'} 1_{d|L_j}]` (tensor signs,
  all root-collision states, the same `λ`).

  recombined inside `|B|²`: `M_new ≤ C_Λ(h) · principalSifted`, for the SAME weight (V21 quadratic
  domination; uses only nonnegative divisor sums of `Λ_new^+`).
- `GoodPrimeEulerFactor.eulerFactor_eq_local_average` — `E_p(s,t) = 1 + 1/(p-2) Σ_k
  (p^{-s_k-t_k} - p^{-s_k} - p^{-t_k})` is the local average of the signed square;
  `signed_square_zero_is_avoidance` — at zero parameters the signed square is the indicator that
  all spectator forms avoid `p`; `eulerFactor_zero`.

# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V25 report: fixed-modulus localization repair

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős Problem #287 remains OPEN.**  Nothing in this bank is
a proof of #287; no explicit `M₀` is produced and no finite splice is performed.

Mode: APPEND-ONLY / POST-ASTRA / SOURCE-LITERAL / PROVIDER-MINIMIZATION / NO EFFECTIVITY YET.
Research Banks V2–V24, every historical report and `ARISTOTLE_SUMMARY.md` are untouched
(verified by `git diff --name-status a08308e HEAD`, see §Git audit).

Status classes used (only): LEAN BANK, LEAN CONDITIONAL, EXTERNAL PROVIDER, FINITE REGRESSION,
REPAIRED / RETIRED, OPEN (Lean: `ResearchBankV25.Ledger.StatusClass`).

Principal update realised here: the fixed exceptional modulus is repaired by an EXACT centering
identity whose correction term carries an algebraically generated `1/φ(q)`, an exact conditioned
residue-energy contraction (arbitrary complex masses, overlapping moduli), the coprime
localized-energy reindexing, good-modulus affine clearing, and the two historical counterfixtures.

## Files and contents

### `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV25/FixedModulusCentering.lean`

For a modulus `q`, a residue `a` and an integer `v` put

    δ(q, a, v) = 1_{v ≡ a (mod q)} − 1_{gcd(v, q) = 1} / φ(q).

**LEAN BANK.**

* `full_centering_fixed_modulus_exact` — for coprime `f, q` and any `r` with `r ≡ c (mod f)`,
  `r ≡ a (mod q)` (i.e. `r = CRT(c, a)`), and for EVERY integer `v` (units and non-units alike):

      δ(fq, r, v) = 1_{v ≡ c (f)} δ(q, a, v) + [1_{gcd(v,q)=1}/φ(q)] δ(f, c, v).

  The unit hypotheses `c ∈ (ℤ/f)^×`, `a ∈ (ℤ/q)^×` of the Astra statement are NOT needed: the
  identity is purely a CRT / totient-multiplicativity identity, so it is proved without them.
* `centered_sum_split` — the summed form for an arbitrary finitely supported complex coefficient:
  the full-modulus discrepancy splits into the localized discrepancy plus the correction whose
  reciprocal weight `1/φ(q)` is produced by the identity itself.
* `correction_term_needed` (regression) — deleting the correction term is FALSE.

Theorems (6): `indMod_mul`, `indCop_mul`, `indMod_congr`, `full_centering_fixed_modulus_exact`, `correction_term_needed`, `centered_sum_split`

Definitions / structures: `def indMod`, `def indCop`, `def delta`, `def CorrectionDeletable`

### `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV25/FixedResidueEnergy.lean`

All statements allow ARBITRARY complex residue masses `z_r`.  `‖w‖²` is written
`Complex.normSq w`.

**LEAN BANK.**

* `fibre_pythagoras` — abstract projection identity.  For a finite set of residues `R`, a
  fibre map `π : R → U` all of whose fibres have the same cardinality `k`, arbitrary masses `z`
  and an arbitrary centre `c` (e.g. the full average), with `D_r = z_r − c` and conditioned
  discrepancy `E_r = z_r − (1/k) Σ_{π s = π r} z_s`:

      Σ_r |E_r|² = Σ_r |D_r|² − (1/k) Σ_u |Σ_{π r = u} D_r|².

* `conditioned_energy_le` — hence conditioned energy ≤ full-modulus energy.
* `overlap_fibre_card` / `overlap_pythagoras` — the general overlapping-modulus instance: `R` is
  `(ℤ/m)^×` with `m` any multiple of `f` (e.g. `m = lcm(f,q)`), `π` the reduction to `(ℤ/f)^×`;
  every fibre (the compatible fibre `A_u`) has the same size `k` with `k · φ(f) = φ(m)`.
* `product_pythagoras` / `coprime_conditioned_energy_le` — the coprime instance on
  `(ℤ/f)^× × (ℤ/q)^×` (`g = 1`, `k = φ(q)`).
* `localized_discrepancy_eq` — for `α_u(n) = α(n) 1_{n ≡ u (f)}`, the literal localized
  discrepancy `Δ_{α_u}(q,a)` equals the conditioned discrepancy `E_{u,a}` of the residue masses
  `z(u,a) = Σ_{n ≡ u (f), n ≡ a (q)} α(n)`.
* `full_discrepancy_eq` — the literal full-modulus discrepancy `Δ_α(fq, r)` equals `D_{CRT(r)}`.
* **`localized_energy_le_full`** — `Σ_u Σ_a |Δ_{α_u}(q,a)|² ≤ Σ_r |Δ_α(fq,r)|²`.
* `divisor_reindexing` — `Σ_{q≤U} τ(q)^J S(q) ≤ Σ_{ℓ≤fU} τ(ℓ)^J T(ℓ)` whenever
  `S(q) ≤ T(fq)` and `T ≥ 0` (using `τ(q) ≤ τ(fq)`).

**Semantic firewall.**  `α_u` is NOT asserted to be globally Siegel–Walfisz anywhere; only the
full-modulus energy of `α` is ever consumed.  The final BDH saving for that energy is the
EXTERNAL PROVIDER `BDHEnergyProvider` of `LocalizationContract.lean`.

Theorems (18): `fibre_one`, `fibre_pythagoras`, `conditioned_energy_le`, `overlap_fibre_card`, `overlap_pythagoras`, `prod_fibre_card`, `prod_fibre_sum`, `product_pythagoras`, `coprime_conditioned_energy_le`, `sum_units_ite`, `sum_units_prod_ite`, `coprime_iff_isUnit`, `localized_discrepancy_eq`, `crtUnits_val`, `natCast_eq_iff`, `full_discrepancy_eq`, `localized_energy_le_full`, `divisor_reindexing`

### `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV25/Counterfixtures.lean`

**A. Residue restriction does not preserve a global SW statement.**  The constant sequence
`α ≡ 1` on `[1, 6]` is exactly balanced modulo `3` (`Δ_α(3, a) = 0` for every residue class),
but its restriction `α_1 = α · 1_{n ≡ 1 (3)}` to ONE fixed residue class has
`Δ_{α_1}(3, 1) = 2 − 2/2 = 1 ≠ 0`.  (`const_sequence_balanced`,
`restricted_sequence_unbalanced`, `residue_restriction_breaks_SW`.)

**B. A fixed slope can destroy unit status on a bad fixed modulus.**  With `A_i = 2`, `A_j = 3`,
`t = 8`: the prime variable `p = A_i t + 1 = 17` is a unit mod `3`, but `A_j p = 51` is NOT a
unit mod `3`; the good slope `A_i` keeps unit status (`2·17 = 34 ≡ 1`).  (`slope_destroys_unit`.)

Both historical inferences are classified **REPAIRED / RETIRED** (see `Ledger.lean`).

# Erdős #287 — Research Bank V26 report: actual Heath-Brown / rough source adapters

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős Problem #287 remains OPEN.**  Nothing in this bank is
a proof of #287; no explicit `M₀` is produced and no finite splice is performed.

Mode: APPEND-ONLY / POST-ASTRA / SOURCE-LITERAL / PROVIDER-MINIMIZATION / NO EFFECTIVITY YET.
Research Banks V2–V24, every historical report and `ARISTOTLE_SUMMARY.md` are untouched
(verified by `git diff --name-status a08308e HEAD`, see §Git audit).

Status classes used (only): LEAN BANK, LEAN CONDITIONAL, EXTERNAL PROVIDER, FINITE REGRESSION,
REPAIRED / RETIRED, OPEN (Lean: `ResearchBankV25.Ledger.StatusClass`).

Exact rough/Heath-Brown source identities and the source-level (not merely length-level) HB
branch coverage; the analytic tail and product-boundary estimates are explicit providers.

## Files and contents

### `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV26/RoughConvolution.lean`

For `z ∈ ℕ` put

    R_z(n) = 1_{P⁻(n) ≥ z}   (every prime factor of n is ≥ z; R_z(1) = 1),
    H_z(d) = 1_{P⁺(d) < z}   (every prime factor of d is < z; H_z(1) = 1),

both zero at `0`.  `H_z` is the indicator of ALL `z`-smooth integers, prime powers included — it is
NOT silently replaced by its squarefree part.

**LEAN BANK.**

* `primeIndicator_isMultiplicative` — `n ↦ 1_{n ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ p ∣ n, P p}` is multiplicative;
* **`rough_mu_identity`** — `μ · R_z = μ ⋆ H_z` (as arithmetic functions);
* **`rough_one_identity`** — `R_z = 1 ⋆ (μ · H_z)`;
* `rough_mu_identity_apply`, `rough_one_identity_apply` — the pointwise divisor-sum forms
  `μ(n) R_z(n) = Σ_{d ∣ n} μ(d) H_z(n/d)` and `R_z(n) = Σ_{d ∣ n} μ(d) H_z(d)`.

Theorems (9): `primeIndicator_apply`, `primeIndicator_isMultiplicative`, `primeIndicator_prime_pow`, `sum_antidiag_prime_pow`, `moebius_prime_pow'`, `rough_mu_identity`, `rough_one_identity`, `rough_mu_identity_apply`, `rough_one_identity_apply`

Definitions / structures: `def primeIndicator`, `def R`, `def H`

### `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV26/HeathBrownIdentity.lean`

Let `M_y(n) = μ(n) 1_{n ≤ y}` (real-valued arithmetic function).  All convolutions are Dirichlet
convolutions in the commutative ring `ArithmeticFunction ℝ`.

**LEAN BANK.**

* `hb_ring_identity` — for every `k`, the exact ring identity
  `Λ = (1 − 1⋆M_y)^k ⋆ Λ + Σ_{j<k} (−1)^j C(k, j+1) · (M_y^{⋆(j+1)} ⋆ 1^{⋆j} ⋆ log)`
  (binomial theorem + `Λ ⋆ 1 = log`);
* `one_sub_zeta_My` — `1 − 1⋆M_y = 1⋆(μ − M_y)`, a function supported on `n > y`;
* `pow_supported` — `(1⋆(μ − M_y))^{⋆k}` is supported on `n > y^k` (`k ≥ 1`, `y ≥ 0`);
* **`heath_brown_identity`** — for `n ≤ y^k` (`k ≥ 1`, `y ≥ 0`):

      Λ(n) = Σ_{j=1}^{k} (−1)^{j−1} C(k, j) (M_y^{⋆j} ⋆ 1^{⋆(j−1)} ⋆ log)(n)

  (written with `j ↦ j+1`, `j < k`);
* `heath_brown_k3` — the instance `k = 3`;
* `hb_k3_at_most_six_variables` — every `k = 3` term has `j + (j−1) + 1 ≤ 6` convolution
  factors; missing factors are the singleton sequence `{1}` (see `SingletonBins.lean`).

No requirement that any rough bin contain a value `> x^ν` is made.

Theorems (12): `My_apply`, `Mb_apply_ne_zero`, `one_sub_zeta_My`, `supportedAbove_mul`, `zeta_Mb_supported`, `pow_supported`, `vanish_of_supported`, `dlt_mul_apply`, `hb_ring_identity`, `heath_brown_identity`, `heath_brown_k3`, `hb_k3_at_most_six_variables`

Definitions / structures: `def My`, `def Mb`, `def SupportedAbove`, `def dlt`, `def hbTerm`, `def hbCoeff`, `def evalAt`

### `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV26/RoughSWAdapter.lean`

## §4.2  Truncated smooth-divisor tail

`R_z(n) = Σ_{d ∣ n} μ(d) H_z(d)` (V26 §4.1).  Truncating at `d ≤ y` leaves the error
`E_y(n) = Σ_{d ∣ n, d > y} μ(d) H_z(d)`.

**LEAN BANK.**
* `rough_truncation_split` — `R_z(n) = Σ_{d∣n, d≤y} μ(d)H_z(d) + E_y(n)` exactly;
* `truncation_error_le` — `Σ_{n ≤ N} |E_y(n)| ≤ N · Σ_{y < d ≤ N} H_z(d)/d`.  The count of
  multiples is `⌊N/d⌋ ≤ N/d`; NO extra `+1` per divisor is inserted.

**EXTERNAL PROVIDER.**
* `SmoothTailProvider` — the Rankin-type reciprocal tail
  `Σ_{d > y, P⁺(d) < z} 1/d ≤ exp(−(log log x)²) log^C x`.

**LEAN CONDITIONAL.**
* `truncation_error_conditional` — the absolute source error is at most
  `N · exp(−(log log x)²) log^C x`.

## §4.4  Source sequence types

`RoughMuSequence`, `RoughOneSequence`, `RoughLogSequence`, `ComplementaryDivisorBoundedSequence`
are concrete coefficient sequences.  One-boundedness (`OneBounded`), rough support
(`RoughSupported`), an SW property and an `L²` divisor bound are SEPARATE predicates.

**Firewall (LEAN BANK).**  `rough_does_not_imply_SW`: a one-bounded, rough-supported sequence
(the indicator of `{1}`) is NOT balanced modulo `3`; so no implication `rough ⟹ SW` exists.

Theorems (11): `rough_truncation_split`, `H_nonneg_le_one`, `truncation_error_le`, `truncation_error_conditional`, `R_values`, `roughMu_oneBounded`, `roughMu_roughSupported`, `roughOne_oneBounded`, `roughOne_roughSupported`, `roughLog_roughSupported`, `rough_does_not_imply_SW`

Definitions / structures: `def truncErr`, `structure SmoothTailProvider`, `def OneBounded`, `def RoughSupported`, `def L2DivisorBound`, `def RoughMuSequence`, `def RoughOneSequence`, `def RoughLogSequence`, `structure ComplementaryDivisorBoundedSequence`, `def deltaOne`

### `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV26/ProductIntervalBoxes.lean`

Dyadicization alone does NOT remove the product constraint `x < m₁⋯m_k ≤ 2x`.  We use
multiplicative boxes of ratio `1 + h` (`h = log^{-B} x`):
`B = ∏_i [L_i, L_i(1+h))`.  A box is INTERIOR if `x < ∏ L_i` and `∏ L_i (1+h)^k ≤ 2x`,
EXTERIOR if `∏ L_i (1+h)^k ≤ x` or `2x < ∏ L_i`, and BOUNDARY otherwise.

**LEAN BANK.**
* `interior_rectangular` — on an interior box the product cutoff is identically `1`, so the
  constraint is RECTANGULAR there;
* `exterior_zero` — on an exterior box it is identically `0`;
* `box_decomposition` — exact decomposition of the cut sum into interior rectangular sums plus
  ONE sum over the UNION of boundary boxes.

**EXTERNAL PROVIDER.**
* `ProductBoundaryProvider` — the analytic boundary estimate
  `O(x √h log^C x + x^{1/2} log^C x)` for the union of boundary products.

**LEAN CONDITIONAL.**
* `product_boxing_conditional` — the cut sum equals the interior rectangular sums up to the
  provider bound, applied ONCE (no factor `#boxes`).
* `boundary_bound_not_multiplied` (regression) — multiplying by the number of boxes would give a
  strictly larger bound as soon as there are two boundary boxes.

Theorems (6): `prod_bounds`, `interior_rectangular`, `exterior_zero`, `box_decomposition`, `product_boxing_conditional`, `boundary_bound_not_multiplied`

Definitions / structures: `structure MulBox`, `def MulBox.Mem`, `def productCut`, `def Interior`, `def Exterior`, `structure BoxingData`, `def BoxingData.cutSum`, `def BoxingData.interiorSum`, `def BoxingData.boundarySum`, `structure ProductBoundaryProvider`

### `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV26/SingletonBins.lean`

A Heath-Brown term with fewer than six variables is padded with the singleton sequence `{1}`
(the Dirichlet unit `δ₁ = 1`), which changes nothing.  No rough bin is required to contain a
value `> x^ν`: the singleton bin contains only `1`.

**LEAN BANK.**
* `singleton_apply` — `δ₁(n) = 1_{n = 1}`;
* `pad_singleton` — `F ⋆ δ₁^{⋆m} = F` for every `m`;
* `hb_term_six_variables` — every `k = 3` HB term equals a product of EXACTLY six factors after
  padding with singleton sequences;
* `singleton_bin_values` — the singleton bin's only nonzero value is at `n = 1`, so no lower
  bound `> x^ν` on bin values is available or needed.

Theorems (4): `singleton_apply`, `pad_singleton`, `hb_term_six_variables`, `singleton_bin_values`

### `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV26/DyadicSourceMap.lean`

**LEAN BANK.**
* `dyadic_mem` / `dyadic_unique` — every `n ≥ 1` lies in exactly one dyadic interval
  `[2^k, 2^{k+1})`, namely `k = ⌊log₂ n⌋`;
* `dyadic_partition_of_unity` — `Σ_{k<K} 1_{[2^k,2^{k+1})}(n) = 1` for `1 ≤ n < 2^K`;
* `dyadicBox` / `source_sum_by_boxes` — for any finite set of variable tuples and any source
  coefficient `F`, `Σ_m F(m) = Σ_{boxes b} Σ_{m ∈ box b} F(m)`: every source term is counted in
  exactly one dyadic box (source-level, not a length census).

Dyadicization alone does NOT remove the product constraint `x < m₁⋯m_k ≤ 2x`; that is the job of
the multiplicative boxes (`ProductIntervalBoxes.lean`).

Theorems (4): `dyadic_mem`, `dyadic_unique`, `dyadic_partition_of_unity`, `source_sum_by_boxes`

Definitions / structures: `def dyadicBox`

### `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV26/HBBranchCoverage.lean`

Each HB term has at most six variables; a dyadic box assigns to each variable a length exponent
`e_i ≥ 0` with `Σ e_i = 1` (normalised by `log x`).

**LEAN BANK.**
* `greedy_subset_sum` — if every step is `≤ c` and the target window `[L, U]` has length
  `≥ c`, a sub-sum lands in the window;
* **`branch_trichotomy`** — for `0 < α ≤ 2/5`, every length vector is
  TYPE II (some sub-product has length in `[α, 1−α]`), ONE-LARGE (a single variable
  `> 1−α`) or TWO-LARGE (two variables with total `> 1−α`);
* `trichotomy_fails_beyond` (regression) — at `α = 12/25 > 2/5` five equal variables `1/5`
  are in none of the three classes, so the threshold matters;
* `BranchRecord` — the actual branch record (source coefficient, selected Type-II variables,
  complementary variables, roughness, one-bounded / `L²` status, length, dyadic box, provider);
* `classify` / `classify_spec` — every box receives a record whose provider condition HOLDS;
* **`source_level_coverage`** — every source term of the HB sum is counted exactly once, in
  exactly one branch:  `Σ_m F(m) = Σ_{kind} Σ_{boxes b of this kind} Σ_{m ∈ b} F(m)`.

Theorems (5): `greedy_subset_sum`, `branch_trichotomy`, `trichotomy_fails_beyond`, `classify_spec`, `source_level_coverage`

Definitions / structures: `def TypeII`, `def OneLarge`, `def TwoLarge`, `inductive BranchKind`, `inductive SourceKind`, `inductive SizeStatus`, `structure BranchRecord`, `def RecordValid`, `def classify`

### `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV26/BoundaryBudget.lean`

With `L = log x` and `h = L^{-B}` the provider bound `x √h L^C + x^{1/2} L^C` is at most
`2 x L^{-A}` once `B ≥ 2(C + A)` and `L^{C+A} ≤ x^{1/2}`.

**LEAN BANK** (exact real-exponent arithmetic):
* `sqrt_rpow_neg` — `√(L^{-B}) = L^{-B/2}`;
* `boundary_first_term` — `x √(L^{-B}) L^C ≤ x L^{-A}` for `B ≥ 2(C+A)`, `L ≥ 1`;
* `boundary_second_term` — `x^{1/2} L^C ≤ x L^{-A}` when `L^{C+A} ≤ x^{1/2}`;
* `boundary_budget` — the sum is `≤ 2 x L^{-A}`.

Theorems (4): `sqrt_rpow_neg`, `boundary_first_term`, `boundary_second_term`, `boundary_budget`

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY.  **Erdős Problem #287 remains OPEN.**  Nothing in this bank is
a proof of #287; no explicit `M₀` is produced and no finite splice is performed.

### `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV27/AxiomAudit.lean`

`#print axioms` for every theorem of the bank (76 theorems).

Aggregator: `RequestProject/Erdos287/ResearchBankV27.lean` (imports every file above).

## Notes, deviations and honest caveats

* Files use ordinary (non-`module`) Lean headers, exactly like the frozen banks V2–V24, so that they
  import the frozen banks unchanged.
* **DI class restriction (important).**  A provider quantified over ALL admissible Kloosterman data
  is provably FALSE (`unrestricted_provider_false`, via an explicit degenerate admissible form with
  `Ξ = 0`).  `DISpectralProvider η DIClass` therefore quantifies over a class `DIClass` of genuine DI
  forms, and each realized clean form must be certified to lie in `DIClass`
  (`CleanAdmissible`).  This keeps the provider satisfiable in principle and makes the certification
  obligation explicit.
* The master bound is stated with `N_q` in place of `N²/Q` and with the representation/diagonal loss
  written as `x^ε`; the conservative bound carries the explicit constant `√3`
  (`|W| ≤ √3 N_q x^{−η}`).
* Representation moment: the finite combinatorics (`bPsi_norm_le`, `bPsi_L2_le`,
  `same_rep_relation`, `diagonal_count_le`) are LEAN BANK; the divisor-type moment bound itself is
  `RepresentationMomentProvider` (LEAN CONDITIONAL row).
* The real-correction exponent `−1079/1900` is recorded as the supplied value; its derivation from

### 4.5  Valuation lift

* `valuationLift_mul` : `ℓ^{e₀}·(ℓ^v d₀) = ℓ^{e₀+v}·d₀`, i.e. `q d = h d₀` with `h = ℓ^{e₀+v}`;
* `valuationLift_floor` : `⌊⌊M/q⌋ / ℓ^v⌋ = ⌊M/h⌋`;
* `valuationLift_unit_cofactor` : `d₀` is prime to `ℓ` and bounded by the lifted height.

### 4.6  `p`-adic layer saturation (local step)

`ContactCore/PadicSaturation.lean`:

* `subsetSums_card_ge` : the subset sums of `k` nonzero residues have size `≥ min(ℓ, k+1)`;
* `subsetSums_eq_univ` : **subset sums of any `ℓ-1` nonzero residues cover `𝔽_ℓ`** (proved
  directly; Cauchy–Davenport is not needed);
* `padicLayer_hits_target` : the digit step actually consumed at a valuation layer;
* `heavy_obstruction_charged`, `sparse_obstruction_small` : the two branches of the PP obstruction
  dichotomy.

The **global** (PADIC-SAT) statement — `|C_v \ P| ≥ ℓ-1` at every layer implies `P` extends to a
complete legal row state — is recorded as the uninhabited `Prop` `PadicSaturationStatement`
(`status = open`, `evidence = researchConjecture`).  Only its layer-local digit step is
kernel-proved.

## Corrected step (audit finding)

The requested chain

```
asinh(X^400) < log(2 X^400) < 401 log X
```

has a **false first step**: `arsinh t = log(t + √(1+t²)) > log(2t)` for every `t > 0`, since
`√(1+t²) > t`.  This is recorded and kernel-proved as
`September2OneSlotPerron.arsinh_gt_log_two_mul`.  The chain is repaired with the constant
`5/2` in place of `2` (valid because `√(1+t²) ≤ (3/2)t` for `t ≥ 1`), which yields exactly the
intended conclusion `perronMassOne X < 128 log X` for `X ≥ 3` (using `401 < 128π`).

rewritten, weakened, or reinterpreted.  No new analytic prime-distribution theorem is
asserted anywhere.  Maynard Theorem 1.1, Bombieri–Vinogradov, Wright and Bordignon–Lee are
**not** asserted, and are not represented even as fields — the only analytic input is an
external hypothesis socket for which this development constructs **no inhabitant**.
Erdős #287 is **not** claimed; it stays `open`.

## 3. Exact source statements formalised

**(a) Finite extension.**  Semantically identical to the pre-existing finite-bank theorem
(`Erdos287.Gap2CE.no_of_M_le_4e9`, `Erdos287.no_Erdos287Counterexample_of_max_le_4e9`),
with the ceiling extended:

```
Gap2CE.no_of_M_le_extendedCeiling :
  ∀ (ce : Gap2CE), 3 ≤ ce.M → ce.M ≤ 67108856338751594 → False

no_Erdos287Counterexample_of_max_le_extendedCeiling :
  Erdos287Counterexample A → A.max' _ ≤ 67108856338751594 → False

arithmeticCoverage_exceeds_twoExp375 : 38643198608805673 < extendedCeiling
```

The same `Gap2CE` / `Erdos287Counterexample` predicates and the same interval blocker
`Gap2CE.blocker_window` are used; only the certificate data is new.  This is **not** a
different arithmetic statement with a similar endpoint.

**(b) 2-adic Möbius pairing.**  `μ(2a) = −μ(a)` for odd `a`; the canonical coefficients
`kappaEps w d = μ(d)·w(d)` and `sigmaEps w m = μ(m)·w(oddPart m)` satisfy the two explicit
pairing equations; and, with `Y` the supplied split datum for `n^γ`,

```
∑_{m ∣ n, m ≤ Y, 4 ∤ m} σ(m)
  = ∑_{d ∣ n, d odd} κ(d) · ( 1_{d ≤ Y} − 1_{2d ∣ n} · 1_{2d ≤ Y} )
```

with the indicators written as Lean `if _ then 1 else 0` inside Finset-filtered sums.  The
two pairing equations are **explicit hypotheses** of the theorem (and proved for the
canonical coefficient) — nothing load-bearing is hidden inside an unconstrained structure.

**(c) Split identity.**  `totSource = totSourceFamily0 − totSourceFamily2`, with
family 0 = `{d odd, d ∣ n, d ≤ Y n}` and family 2 = `{d odd, 2d ∣ n, 2d ≤ Y n}`, for
supplied physical weights; no absolute value occurs in the identity.  A separate algebraic
witness (`termwise_triangle_loses_pairing`) exhibits an instance where the paired sum is `0`
while the termwise absolute sum is `2`.

**(d) Fixed-residue arithmetic.**
`(2dr + s) ≡ s [ZMOD d]`; `(4du + s) ≡ s [ZMOD 4d]`; and, under `p` odd, `d` odd, `s = ±1`,
`p ≡ s [ZMOD d] → 2d ∣ p − s` (equivalently `∃ u, p = 2du + s`).  Parity hypotheses are not
weakened.

**(e) Conditional compiler.**
`PhysicalFixedResidueAPBound F → |E_T F w A| ≤ ∑_{slots} |w d| · err(slot)`, with slot index
`D ×ˢ {1,4} ×ˢ {−1,+1}` (`slotIndex_card = 4·|D|`, `slotIndex_fiber_card = 4`).

## 5. Uninhabited analytic sockets

* `Erdos287.September3ConditionalCompiler.PhysicalFixedResidueAPBound` — the *only* analytic
  input of this layer.  Exposed fields: per-slot **prime discrepancy**, **numerical error
  function** `err`, the **bound** `|discrepancy| ≤ err` quantified over each finite physical
  interval, plus `err_nonneg`; the slot itself carries **residue** `s = ±1`, **modulus**
  `q1 · d` with `q1 ∈ {1,4}` and `d` odd, and the **interval endpoints** `lo`, `hi`; the
  **activation threshold** lives in `PhysicalSlotFamily`.  It stores **no** `E_T`
  conclusion and **no** endpoint-supremum field.  No inhabitant is constructed anywhere.
* Pre-existing sockets (complete Perron/nuclear ledger; hard-`U` shared-Ford adapter) are
  untouched and keep their earlier statuses.

Honesty note (also in the module docstring): the socket is deliberately weak — nothing
forces `err` to be small, so a vacuous inhabitant with huge `err` exists in principle.  The
compiler's conclusion is correspondingly symbolic in `err`, and no number is banked.

## 6. Firewalls

1. **FINITE-CERTIFICATE-COVERAGE** is an arithmetic finite result only; it does **not**
   assert that the medium analytic branch is closed
   (`finiteCoverage_does_not_close_medium_branch`).
2. **FIXED-RESIDUE-SOURCE ≠ ANALYTIC-PRIME-DISTRIBUTION-THEOREM** — §C is congruence
   algebra over `ℤ`; `p` is a name, not a primality assumption.
3. The conditional compiler does not assert Maynard or any analytic theorem
   (`maynard_is_not_asserted`).
4. The conditional compiler does not assert a numerical `E_T` bound
   (`maynardNumericalConstant = notBanked`).
5. The conditional compiler does not assert `E_T = o(B_X)` — that would have to be supplied
   separately (`eTDirectedMedium = conditionalOpen`).
6. The conditional compiler does not imply Erdős #287
   (`conditionalCompiler_does_not_prove_erdos287`; `erdos287 = open_`).
7. No endpoint-supremum field is banked (`endpointSupremumField = notBanked`).
8. Status rows are metadata, never proof claims; five rows are additionally backed by the
   theorems they label (`row_*_backed`).

## 3. Exact source identities proved

1. `W(x) = exp(1 − 1/(1 − (10x−8)²))` on `|10x−8| < 1`, `0` elsewhere; `0 ≤ W ≤ 1`;
   `W(7/10) = W(9/10) = 0`; `W(4/5) = 1`; `sSup (range W) = 1`;
   `eVariationOn W univ = 2`; `C_W = 2·1 + 2 = 4`.
2. `κ_ε(d) = μ(d_low)·g_j = (−1)^{ω(d)} = μ(d)` for squarefree `d = d_low·d_high`,
   `ω(d_high) = j`, `g_j = (−1)^j`; and `κ_ε(d_low·p, j) = κ_ε(d_low, j+1)`.
3. `T⁰ − T² = Σ_{r odd} κ·Wt·B_src·1_{d ≤ Y(dr)} + Σ_{r even} κ·Wt·B_src·1_{d ≤ Y(dr) < 2d}`,
   with exact cancellation of every even `r` satisfying `2d ≤ Y(dr)`; the reindexing
   `r = 2u` keeps `n`, `κ`, `Wt`, and (under `B_src(2m) = B_src(m)`) `B_src`.
4. `Σ_{d ∣ q} μ(d) B_src(d) β(q/d) = ∏_{p ∣ q} (β_loc p − B_loc p)` for squarefree `q`;
   under `β_loc p − B_loc p = −S₂` this is `S₂^{ω(q)} μ(q)`.
5. `R_{B,signed} = −4 Σ_{d odd} (E_d[V0,d] − E_d[V2,d])`, the `−4` derived from
   `#{±1} · #{±1} · compareSign = 2·2·(−1)`.
6. `poleBudget + oscillatoryBudget = 14164610/10^15 + 985835/10^12 < 1/10^6`.
7. `9360 L(1+L)e^{−L/2}` strictly decreasing on `[4,∞)`; `envelope(62.5) < 10⁻⁶`.

### Repair found (§4)

The literally requested identity `Σ_{d∣q} μ(d) B_src(d) β(q/d) = S₂·μ(q)` is **false** for
`ω(q) ≥ 2`.  Counterexample (`literal_S2_mu_form_fails`, kernel-proved): `q = 15`,
`S₂ = 2`, `B_loc ≡ 0`, `β_loc ≡ −2`; the local normalisation `β_loc p − B_loc p = −S₂`
holds at both primes, and the divisor sum equals `4 = S₂²·μ(15)`, not `2 = S₂·μ(15)`.
The correct global form is `S₂^{ω(q)}·μ(q)` (`interiorCollapse_normalized`); the requested
shape holds exactly under the explicit extra hypothesis `S₂^{ω(q)} = S₂`
(`interiorCollapse_S2_mu`), in particular on a one-prime fibre
(`interiorCollapse_S2_mu_of_prime`).  Nothing was weakened: both forms are stated, and the
false one is recorded with its counterexample rather than silently repaired.

## B. Verdict on the old `cell_identity`

`K0_CELL_IDENTITY_SOURCE_STILL_EXTERNAL`.

The canonical split and the Ford `G_*` definition are not encoded (see archaeology above),
so the specialization "on the `k = 0`, `J = ∅` smooth branch with `σ = ν₀ − 2ε`,
`γ = 1/2 − ε`, `P⁺(n) ≤ n^σ`, the high-prime component is empty and `H_*(n)` reduces to
`∑_{d ∣ n, d ≤ n^γ} μ(d)`" cannot be *proved*; it could only be assumed.  Therefore:

* no fake Ford factorisation definition was introduced;
* the `cell_identity` field is left uninhabited;
* the missing statement is named exactly as `Erdos287.Singleton.K0CellIdentitySource`;
* every downstream theorem carries it as an explicit antecedent.

  necessarily a prime); window `⌊M/q⌋` (floor); the **strict** inequality `C ⌊M/q⌋ < p`
  (threshold on the *base* `p`, not on `q`); `A ⊆ [1,M]`, all elements positive,
  reciprocal sum `1`.  The hypothesis `p^e ≤ M` is present but unused (documented in the
  archive).  There is no coprimality-to-another-parameter, parity or endpoint hypothesis.
* It excludes **every multiple** of `q`, hence both `q` and `2q`.

## D/E. The V1 plus/minus Sophie blockers — proved

* `Erdos287.Gap2CE.plus_sophie_blocker` : `q` prime, `q > 3`, `p = 2q+1` prime, `p ≤ M`,

Every inequality of the intended chain was proved in the archive's own `ℕ` ordering (no
coercion): `M < 3q ⟹ ⌊M/q⌋ ≤ 2`; `M < 3q < 2p`; `M < 3q < 2(p-1)` (plus case) resp.
`M < 2p` (minus case) for placement; and `p-1, p` (resp. `p, p+1`) verified to lie in the
closed window `[N,M]` on which `holes_isolated` applies.  These are strictly stronger than
the banked `safePrime_blocker` (`r > 25 = C 4` plus a placement hypothesis), because the band
hypothesis `M < 3q` sharpens the window from `2d = 4` to `2`.

the maximal band is populated for all `39 ≤ M ≤ 3000` was exploratory only; the
*kernel-verified* range is `39 ≤ M ≤ 250`.

**Repair recorded (statement fix).**  `halfRange_min_le` is **false without `2 ≤ M`**:
`A = {1}` satisfies every field of `Gap2CE` (its single element is the maximum, so `hgap`
is vacuous) and there `N = 1 > 0 = ⌊M/2⌋`.  The hypothesis `2 ≤ M` is included and is
automatically available in every downstream use.

## Conventions fixed by §65 (read before using the numbers)

A cell carries one low exponent `a` and four high exponents `h i`, with
`0 < a ≤ 1/10`, `1/5 ≤ h i ≤ 3/10`, `a + Σ h i = 1`.  The low prime is *pinned* to the fixed
side, so a divisor assignment is a subset `S` of the four high primes with exponent
`σ S = Σ_{i∈S} h i`.  With window half-width `δ` and collar half-width `δ'`
(`0 < δ < δ' ≤ 1/10`):

```
N1 = #{S : 1/2 − δ' ≤ σ S < 1/2 − δ}     (lower collar, half-open)
N2 = #{S : 1/2 − δ  ≤ σ S ≤ 1/2 + δ}     (product window, closed)
N3 = #{S : 1/2 + δ  <  σ S ≤ 1/2 + δ'}   (upper collar, half-open)
H  = N2 − N1 − N3
```

**8 October 2026 | Independent written mathematical audit — NOT a Lean kernel certificate**

## Scope and provenance

Examined the user's previously supplied Aristotle tar archive (`output-final_aristotle/RequestProject/Erdos287/SourceChain/Physical/`) and the user's later Aristotle completion report. The main additional written result below is a *source-specific mixed-parity support lemma*. It has not been translated to a completed, compiled Lean proof.

## Theorem A — complete actual modulus lies in the upper Rosser–Iwaniec support

Fix a scalar sector `(J,P)` with `BoxAdm J P`, a labelled tuple of pairwise distinct high primes `q = (q_1,...,q_J)` from the assigned high boxes, and a nonzero low-sieve coefficient `κ_J(b)`. Assume `ScalarParams.Good` (in particular `X>1`, `T>=2`). Set

\[
D_{\rm hi}:=D_{\rm int}^{1+\tau},\quad
D_{\rm low}:=D_{\rm int}^{e_0},\quad
D_{\rm tot}=D_{\rm hi}D_{\rm low}=X^{59/100},\quad
d=b\prod_{i=1}^Jq_i.
\]

The high primes are all greater than `u_0` and the distinct low primes of `b` are all strictly less than `u_0`, so the two prime groups have disjoint supports. Let the high primes sorted decreasingly be `Q_1>...>Q_J`, and low primes be `r_1>...>r_t`. Since the box list is weakly decreasing and every actual prime is at most its box upper endpoint, the **sorted** high list is pointwise at most the weakly decreasing box upper endpoint list `U_1>=...>=U_J` (repeated boxes are permitted). This pointwise sorting lemma is a necessary separate Lean obligation.

- If a global odd index `k` satisfies `k<=J`, the existing `boxVec_vecHyp` gives

  \[
  Q_1\cdots Q_{k-1}Q_k^3\le U_1\cdots U_{k-1}U_k^3
  \le D_{\rm hi}\le D_{\rm tot}.
  \]

- If a global odd index `k=J+s` has `s>=1`, all high primes precede the low primes and the needed expression is

  \[
  \Bigl(\prod_{i=1}^JQ_i\Bigr)
  r_1\cdots r_{s-1}r_s^3.
  \]

  If `J` is even, `s` is odd and `kappa_sector` gives the low `DplusSet(D_low)` bound; if `J` is odd, `s` is even and `kappa_sector` gives the low `DminusSet(D_low)` bound. In either case, `VecHyp.prod_le` bounds the entire high product by `D_hi`, so this expression is `<= D_hi D_low = D_tot`.

Hence **for every actual nonzero scalar atom**

\[
\boxed{d\in\mathcal D^+(D_{\rm tot})=\mathcal D^+(X^{59/100}).}
\]

For `0<κ<10^{-5}`, `59/100 < 3/5 - 50κ`, so by monotonicity of the support threshold,

\[
\boxed{d\in\mathcal D^+(X^{3/5-50\kappa}).}
\]

For avoidance of doubt, the coarse inequality `d <= D_tot` alone is insufficient: e.g. `14 <= 100` but the largest-prime odd-prefix test fails because `7^3 > 100`. The extra parity-sensitive low/high structure is essential.

This establishes at the written-mathematics level the precise **actual-modulus membership** that the latest Aristotle report leaves unproved. It does **not** grant the convolutional factor independence needed by Proposition 4.4: for that one must retain the already proved **box-fixed** `atomColour`, signed `ellX_tensor`, low/high disjointness, and coefficient one-boundedness. One cannot freely use an independently chosen colouring for each `d` to create a factorized global coefficient.

### Suggested Lean interface (statements only; no kernel proof claimed)

- `actual_high_sorted_majorized`: the sorted list of prime factors of `∏q_i` is entrywise bounded by sorted `boxTop(P i)` (including repeated boxes).
- `Dplus_append_of_parity`: concatenating a high `Dplus` prime list of length `J` and a smaller low `Dplus` list when `Even J`, or a low `Dminus` list when `Odd J`, yields `Dplus` at product of support levels.

- `actual_modulus_Dplus_pascadi`: monotonicity to `X^(3/5-50κ)` for `0<κ<10^-5`.

These statements use the **exact** source index and weight predicates, not a new abstract sieve coefficient.

**Lean-efficient implementation:** work first with the `Finset` of actual high/low prime factors. For a high prime `p`, the `above` set in the full modulus contains precisely the larger high primes; for a low prime `p`, it is the disjoint union of *all* high primes and the larger low primes. Therefore

\[
\#\mathrm{above}_{d}(p)=J+\#\mathrm{above}_{b}(p)
\]

for low `p`, which translates the `Even J`/`Odd J` switch into the exact `DplusSet`/`DminusSet` split. This may be more robust than first proving complete `primeFactorsList` concatenation, especially with repeated high boxes. After the `Finset` theorem, transfer it to `Factor.InDplus` using squarefreeness and the sorted prime list.

**Uniform-in-X variation safeguard:** the number of high boxes is mathematically independent of `X` once `T` is fixed, since

\[
D_j=D_{m int}^{e_0^2(1+	au)^j},\quad
D_j\le\sqrt{D_{m int}}\iff e_0^2(1+	au)^j\le	frac12
\]

for `D_int>1`. The right-hand side depends on `T` only. A Lean theorem `H_eq_H_of_same_T` should precede treating the claimed variation bound `∑_{J≤T²} H^J 3^J` as an `X`-independent constant.

## Theorem B — discharge of actual atom parameters

Define

\[
e_0=1/T,\quad\tau=e_0^9,\quad
\beta=\frac{59e_0}{100(1+e_0+e_0^9)},\quad
D_{\rm low}=X^\beta.
\]

For fixed `0<κ<10^-5`, choose any integer `T>max(2,100/κ)` (the choice depends on the fixed κ, not on X). Then

\[
0<\beta<\frac{59}{100T}<\frac{\kappa}{100},\qquad
4\beta<\kappa.
\]

Take the factorization parameter `δ=κ`. For `X>1`,

\[
D_{\rm low}^2=X^{2\beta}\le X^{\kappa/2}=X^{\delta/2}.
\]

For any actual critical cell satisfying `X^(3κ) <= N <= X^(1/3+κ/2)`, we also have

\[
X^{2\delta}\le N/D_{\rm low},\qquad
N\le X^{1/3+\delta}.
\]

The first inequality follows from `N/Dlow >= X^(3κ-β) >= X^(2κ)` because `β<κ`. The second is immediate.

Thus `AtomParams S κ N` and the additional premise of `atom_factorization_clean` are **mathematically discharged by a fixed parameter choice**, provided the actual source parameter-selection theorem is constructed in Lean. Existing `ScalarParams.Good` by itself (`T>=2`, `X>1`) does not imply these claims.

**Analytic exponent translation:** `atom_factorization_clean` yields `Sys53` with parameter `κ/2`. Pascadi Proposition 4.4 needs `Q1<=N x^-ε`, `N²Q2Q3²<=x^(1-15ε)`, `N²Q2^5 Q3²<=x^(2-40ε)`. Taking the original paper's `ε=κ/2000` leaves strict margins: `κ/2>40κ/2000`, hence also `κ/2>15κ/2000`. Dyadic constants require the usual fixed power reserve.

Pascadi [arXiv:2505.00653v2, Proposition 4.4] is **not** conditional on `Dplus` membership. It applies to three **one-bounded unary convolution coefficients** at legal lengths, with a rough/Siegel–Walfisz `alpha_n`, the full original congruence and its fixed residue `a`, and all listed modulus/range conditions. `Dplus` is used by Proposition 5.2 to guarantee allocation, not to license arbitrary correlated coefficients.

They require the separate base-conditioned actual-atom W4 proof/provider described in the user's `Final proof.pdf` or another legitimate theorem. A source factorization alone does not close that extension.

Current remaining deep analytic hypotheses (no claim of discharge): provider for the actual varying-base nonzero Fourier/Poisson remainder; any missing BV/BDH source adaptation, remainders, fundamental-lemma comparisons, `Lambda` to primes and powers, and the seven-block asymptotic consumer. The precise final list depends on the latest actual `Tail287` theorem signature, which was **not** present in the supplied older archive.

## Effective track: universally quantified arithmetic vs prime supply

For `L_h=lcm(1,...,h)`, one can prove the classical explicit inequality `L_h<=4^(h-1)` for every integer `h>=1` by induction using

\[
L_{2n}\mid L_n\binom{2n}n,\qquad
L_{2n+1}\mid L_{n+1}\binom{2n+1}n.
\]

The binomial factors satisfy `C(2n,n)<=4^n`, `C(2n+1,n)<=4^n`. The existing (latest reported, not in archive) Lean hypothesis `L_h<=3^h` is **not** discharged by testing only `h<=40`. Replace it by an actually proved `4^(h-1)` estimate and adjust the exponent budget.

For the much narrower reported `onset_exp : M>=exp 12 -> H_*(M)>=10`, a separate short proof does **not** need the full lcm exponential theorem: `L_10=2520`, `B_10=7381`, so `10 B_10=73810<exp 12`; monotonicity of `h B_h` yields `H_*(M)>=10` whenever `M>=exp 12`. This is a shortcut for that result only; it does not establish the growing-height `h=floor(log M/2)` theorem.

The exact V103 one-draw object is

\[
\nu_p=\sum_{q\mid p-1}\frac{v_q(p-1)\log q}{\log(p-1)}\delta_{\log q/\log(p-1)},\quad
\nu_M=\frac1{\#\{p:M/2<p\le M\}}\sum_{M/2<p\le M,\ p\text{ prime}}\nu_p,
\]

\[
\eta_M=\frac{\log(K_*(M)+1)}{\log M},\qquad
T_M=\int_{[0,1]}(u-1+\eta_M)_+\,d\nu_M(u).
\]

All occurrences `v_q` (prime multiplicity), odd-prime window, `log(p-1)>0`, `0<eta<1/2` and the strict positivity threshold must appear literally in the Lean predicates. `T_M>0 => not Counterexample287(M)` is an implication; `T_M>0` for all large M, the explicit one-hinge estimate, and finite-bank verification remain **unproved**.

# Erdős #287 — statement-equivalence audit (2026-09-01)

Purpose: check that what the repository calls "the exact public statement" really is the
published problem, and that no formulation used inside the tree is *weaker* than it.

## 1. The published problem

> Let `1 < n₁ < n₂ < ⋯ < n_k` be integers with `∑_{i} 1/n_i = 1`.
> Must some adjacent gap satisfy `n_{i+1} − n_i ≥ 3`?

Three ingredients: (a) a finite strictly increasing sequence of integers `> 1`;
(b) the reciprocal-sum condition `∑ 1/n_i = 1`; (c) the conclusion "some adjacent gap ≥ 3".

## 2. The formal objects

| Informal ingredient | Formal object | File |
|---|---|---|
| candidate counterexample (set form) | `Erdos287.Erdos287Counterexample (A : Finset ℕ)` | `RequestProject/Erdos287/ProblemStatement.lean` |
| public statement (set form) | `Erdos287.Erdos287Statement := ∀ A, ¬ Erdos287Counterexample A` | `RequestProject/Erdos287/ClosureInputs.lean` |
| public statement (ordered form) | `Erdos287.Erdos287SeqStatement` | `RequestProject/Erdos287/OrderedSequenceBridge.lean` |
| historical compiler type | `Erdos287.Gap2CE` | `RequestProject/Erdos287/Counterexample.lean` |

`Erdos287Counterexample A` has exactly four fields:

* `card_ge : 2 ≤ A.card`;
* `one_lt : ∀ a ∈ A, 1 < a`  (ingredient (a): denominators `> 1`);
* `sum_one : ∑ a ∈ A, (1 : ℚ)/a = 1` (ingredient (b));
* `gap_le_two : ∀ a ∈ A, (∃ b ∈ A, a < b) → (a + 1 ∈ A ∨ a + 2 ∈ A)` (negation of (c)).

A `Finset ℕ` is exactly a finite set of distinct integers, i.e. a strictly increasing finite
sequence up to reindexing; `card_ge` only rules out the degenerate one-term "sequence"
`n₁ = 1`, which is excluded anyway by `one_lt` together with `sum_one`.

## 3. The dictionary, formalised

New in this pass (`RequestProject/Erdos287/OrderedSequenceBridge.lean`):

* `Erdos287.enum` — the increasing enumeration of a `Finset ℕ`, i.e. the passage
  set ⟶ ordered sequence; `enum_mem`, `enum_lt_enum`, `exists_enum_eq`, `enum_succ_le`
  (no element lies strictly between consecutive enumeration values), `sum_enum_recip`.
* `erdos287SeqStatement_of_statement` — set form ⇒ ordered form (existing forward bridge
  `erdos287_seq_of_no_counterexample`, repackaged).
* `erdos287Statement_of_seqStatement` — **ordered form ⇒ set form** (new; this was the
  missing direction).
* `erdos287Statement_iff_seqStatement` — `Erdos287Statement ↔ Erdos287SeqStatement`.
  Hence the set formulation is *not* a weakening of the published one.
* `gap_le_two_iff_orderEmb_gap` — the set-level gap field is literally the adjacent-gap
  condition `n_{i+1} ≤ n_i + 2` on the increasing enumeration.
* `sum_recip_rat_iff_real` — the reciprocal-sum condition may be read in `ℚ` or in `ℝ`.

## 4. `Gap2CE` versus the exact predicate

`Gap2CE` is a strict *relaxation* (it allows the denominator `1` and does not demand two
denominators). The bridge is one-way: `Erdos287Counterexample.toGap2CE`. The countermodel
`A = {1}` (`SemanticFirewalls.singletonGap2CE`, `singleton_not_counterexample`) shows the
converse fails. Consequently:

* refuting `Gap2CE` objects is *stronger* than refuting counterexamples — safe direction;
* no theorem stated for `Gap2CE` may be read as a statement about the public problem
  without the bridge.

## 5. Verdict

STATEMENT-EQUIVALENCE AUDIT: **PASS**. The formal statement is the published statement, the
two public formulations are proved equivalent, and the only auxiliary predicate (`Gap2CE`)
is provably a relaxation used in the safe direction. Nothing in the tree weakens the
problem, and Erdős #287 is **not** claimed to be solved.

## C. AFFINE DIVISOR IDENTITY  (Phase B, `PrePoissonDensity3221.lean`)

`Erdos287.PrePoisson3221.isCoprime_two_of_odd` — odd `q` is coprime to `2`.

`Erdos287.PrePoisson3221.affineResidue_iff_dvd_two_mul_add` — **load-bearing**.  For odd `q`
and any `a` with `2a ≡ −s (mod q)`:

```
m·w ≡ a (mod q)   ↔   q ∣ 2·m·w + s
```

`Erdos287.PrePoisson3221.balancedSeven_affine_divisor_condition` — the specialisation to
`s = ±1` used by the balanced-seven source, stated through the predicate `AffineSampled`.

`Erdos287.PrePoisson3221.exists_affineResidue` — the affine residue exists for every odd
`q` (non-vacuity).

No analytic estimate is used or produced.

## D. FIRST CAUCHY / MU-SIGN  (Phase C, `HighConductorVariance3221.lean`)

`Erdos287.HighCond3221.firstCauchy_sign_consumption`:

```
‖∑_q mu(q) X_q‖² ≤ (∑_q mu(q)²) · (∑_q ‖X_q‖²)
```

The right-hand side depends on `mu` **only through `mu(q)²`**.

`postCauchy_weight_sign_invariant` — the post-Cauchy weight is invariant under arbitrary
`q`-wise sign flips `mu ↦ ε·mu`, `ε = ±1`.

`moebius_sq_of_squarefree` — for squarefree `q`, `μ(q)² = 1` (Mathlib result, reused).

`firstCauchy_loses_sign_information` — **firewall**: explicit weight systems with identical
post-Cauchy energies but different pre-Cauchy values.  The original signed `μ(q)` is
provably not retained by the post-Cauchy variance.

Status: `3221-FIRST-CAUCHY-SIGN-CONSUMPTION45 : PROVED_FINITE / PROVED_ALGEBRAIC`.
No Möbius analytic property is formalised or assumed.

`Erdos287.PrePoisson3221.sampled_q_card_le_divisorCount` — any finite family of natural
moduli dividing a fixed nonzero `n` has cardinality `≤ τ(|n|)` (`Nat.divisors` card).
No interval hypothesis is required, so the bound holds for the moduli in **any** interval.

`sampled_q_card_le_divisorCount_affine` — the affine instance: with `q ∣ 2mw + s` and
`2mw + s ≠ 0`, the admissible-`q` count is `≤ τ(|2mw + s|)`.

`τ(n) = X^{o(1)}` is **not** proved and **not** assumed.  It is exposed separately as the

## H. SECOND-COPY COUNT  (Phase E §9)

`secondCopy_shell_iff` — `q ∣ w₁ − w₂ ↔ ∃ t, w₂ = w₁ − q·t`.

`congruence_interval_card_le` — the exact division-free count over `ℤ`:

```
q · #{x ∈ [a, b) : x ≡ r (mod q)} ≤ (b − a) + q      (0 < q, a ≤ b)
```

`congruence_interval_card_le_one_add_quotient` — the floor variant `# ≤ 1 + (b − a)/q`.

`secondCopy_card_le_one_add_quotient` — the shell form for `w₂` in a `ℤ` box.

All statements are `Nat`/`Int` interval theorems; **no informal real interval arithmetic is
used**.

**Combination (Phase E §10):** `sampledQuadBox_card_le`

```
#{(m, w₁, q, w₂)} ≤ (#m)·(#w₁)·divisorMultiplicity·secondCopyMultiplicity
```

with **no `X`-exponent inside the theorem**.

## C. INVERSE-SAMPLED CHARACTER EXPANSION (Phase A)

Module `RequestProject/Erdos287/HighConductorCharacterGram3221.lean`,
namespace `Erdos287.V20Gram`.

The high-conductor character set is **data, not a `Prop` field**: `highSet q Dcut` is the
literal finset `{χ mod q : Dcut < conductor χ}`, characterised by

* `mem_highSet_iff_lt_conductor`
* `sum_highSet_eq_sum_ite`

The affine sample `a_m = −s·(2m)⁻¹ mod q` is the literal definition `affineSample q s m`,
tied to the V19 `samplePoint` by `affineSample_eq_samplePoint`, with

* `affineSample_mul_eq_one`, `affineSample_isUnit`, `affineSample_inv`.

Exact character identity, with the repository's own conjugation convention and **all**
hypotheses explicit (`s² = 1`, `2m` a unit mod `q`):

```lean
theorem inverseSample_character_identity (hs : s ^ 2 = 1)
    (hu : IsUnit ((2 * m : ℕ) : ZMod q)) (chi : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) :
    (starRingEnd ℂ) (chi (affineSample q s m))
      = chi ((-2 * s : ℤ) : ZMod q) * chi ((m : ℕ) : ZMod q)
```

with the unconjugated companion `affineSample_character_factor`, and the supporting
`conj_char_apply`, `conj_char_eq_inv_char`.

High-conductor expansion compiler (§4), with literal character coefficients
`highCoeff q Dcut Wbox c χ = 1_{Dcut < cond χ} · ĉ_q(χ)`:

```lean
theorem cHigh_inverseSampled_expansion :
    cHigh q Dcut Wbox c (affineSample q s m)
      = (q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ * ∑ chi ∈ highSet q Dcut,
          chi ((-2*s : ℤ) : ZMod q) * chi ((m : ℕ) : ZMod q) * cHat q Wbox c chi
```

Every ingredient is a literal Dirichlet-character construction from the repository's own
infrastructure, so:

```lean
theorem inverseSampledVariance_eq_characterGram :
    ∑ q ∈ Qbox, wt q * ∑ m ∈ unitBox q Mset,

            shortMGram q Mset Phi xi * autocorr q (highCoeff q Dcut Wbox c) xi)
```

proved from the per-modulus identity `charSource_variance_eq_gram`. **No Cauchy, no

## C. Why the old HHH closure proof was retracted

The old route decomposed the high–high character sum by a conductor-cell
inclusion–exclusion over quotient conductors and then applied a Burgess-type bound
cell by cell. Two defects make it unusable *as a closure proof*:

1. the inclusion–exclusion cells were indexed by quotient conductors that are not a
   partition of the ambient character set actually used by orthogonality, so the
   decomposition carried an unquantified omitted/overlapping cell risk; and
2. the bad-character count that fed the log budget was the heuristic
   `#Bad_q ≪ D·τ(q)`, which is not a proved finite bound in this repository.

`oldHHH_closure_proof_retracted` records the retraction as kernel-checked status data.
The underlying *representation* is not claimed false, and the V20 objects stay.

The V21 replacement needs no quotient conductor and no conductor-cell
inclusion–exclusion: it is a two-variable indicator identity (section D).

---

## D. Two-high-projector exact algebra

File: `RequestProject/Erdos287/TwoHighProjector3221.lean` (namespace
`Erdos287.V21TwoProj`).

One ambient finite character set `ambientSet α = Finset.univ`, one `Bad : Finset α`,
and `highSetOf Bad = ambientSet α \ Bad`. Indicators `badInd`, `highInd` valued in `ℂ`.

Proved:

* `highIndicator_eq_one_sub_badIndicator : highInd Bad a = 1 - badInd Bad a`
* `twoHighProjector_pointwise :`
  `highInd Bad a * highInd Bad b = 1 - badInd Bad a - badInd Bad b + badInd Bad a * badInd Bad b`
* `highHighSum_eq_AA_sub_BA_sub_AB_add_BB : HH3221 Bad K = AA3221 K - BA3221 Bad K - AB3221 Bad K + BB3221 Bad K`

with the four children defined separately as `AA3221`, `BA3221`, `AB3221`, `BB3221`
(full sums over the *same* ambient set, weighted by the appropriate indicators).

No-omission / no-overlap / no-double-counting are proved explicitly and not left to
prose: `high_bad_disjoint`, `high_union_bad`, `high_card_add_bad_card`,
`twoProjector_no_double_counting`, `sum_eq_indicator_sum`, `HH3221_eq_indicator_sum`.

## B. The safe bad-character log re-ledger

File: `RequestProject/Erdos287/BadCharacterLogLedger3221.lean` (namespace
`Erdos287.V22Ledger`).

The V21 repair replaced the heuristic `#Bad ≪ D·τ(q)` by the proved finite bound
`#Bad ≤ (D+1)²` — **two** powers of the cutoff.  Any compiler whose log arithmetic assumed
one power of `D` is therefore wrong, and V22 re-ledgers it with the cutoff exponent kept
abstract, `D = (log X)^{B0}`:

```
2·AA exponent       = 10
2·BB exponent       = 20 − 8 B0
2·BA (= AB) exponent = 15 − 4 B0
2·C_var(B0)         = min(10, 15 − 4B0, 20 − 8B0)
```

Declarations: `cutoffOfB0`, `cutoffOfB0_eq_sharedCutoff` (it *is* the V21 shared cutoff),
`aaDoubledExponent`, `bb_logExponent`, `ba_logExponent`,
`highProjectorVarianceLogExponent`, `cvar`, `cvar_doubled`, `cvar_le_channels`.

Kernel-checked samples: `cvar_at_one : C_var(1) = 5`, `cvar_at_two : C_var(2) = 2`,
`cvar_at_three : C_var(3) = −2`, and `cvar_decreasing_sample`.  In particular the budget
is genuinely `B0`-dependent and goes **negative** at `B0 = 3`.  `B0 < 5` is nowhere
hard-coded.

# Erdős #287: External provider map (Research Bank V29/V30)

INTERNAL #287 RESEARCH PROGRAMME ONLY. **Erdős #287 is OPEN. Explicit M₀ is OPEN. Finite splice is OPEN.**

This file covers every field of `Erdos287.ResearchBankV29.ProviderElimination.MinimalExternalAnalyticProviders`.

**Honest scope.** The bank defines only some of the objects the fields talk about. The
branch functionals `D0, D1, D2, Db`, the DI class `DIClass`, the principal model `model`, the
universes `E, Psm, Prd`, and `N, Li, phiW` are **theorem parameters**. None of them is built from the
physical #287 source. Where a mapping column below says "parameter", it means this: the variable,
range or coefficient mapping to the cited theorem cannot be checked against the source until that
object is defined. That gap is the SUCCESS D finding of V30.

---

## 1. `rosser : RosserScalarProvider K h F Psm Prd lev X`
- **Lean**: `density : DimensionOneDensity h K`; `F_rosser : ∀ s, 1 ≤ s → s ≤ 3 → F s = 2 e^γ / s`;
  `F_tendsto_one : F S → 1`; `small : ∀ S>0, ∀ ε>0, ∃ x₀, ∀ x ≥ x₀, costU(Psm S x, ellRd(Psm S x, id, lev x), h) ≤ F S + ε`;
  `rough_unrounded : … costU(Prd S x, ellRd(Prd S x, id, X x), h) ≤ F s0 + ε`; `small_nonneg`.
- **Prose**: this is the dimension-one Rosser–Iwaniec upper-bound sieve. Its normalized cost at level `D` tends to `F(s)`, with `F(s) = 2e^γ/s` for `1 ≤ s ≤ 3`.
- **Source**: V22 `RosserCostProvider`, and the V22 report.
- **Variable mapping**: sifting density `h`, dimension-one constant `K`, sieve level `lev x = x^ρ` (ρ = 1/10⁶) for the small primes and `X x = x^{ϑ₀}` (ϑ₀ = 545999/10⁶) for the rough primes.
- **Range / coefficient / normalization**: `Psm, Prd` and `h` are parameters. The cost is `costU` (V22, defined).
- **Effectivity**: effective in principle. No explicit constants are recorded.

## 2. `tuple : PrimeHarmonicTupleProvider h Prd X wτ`
- **Lean**: `rounding : ∀ S>0, ∀ τ>0, ∀ ε>0, ∃ x₀, ∀ x ≥ x₀, costU(rounded ellRd) ≤ costU(unrounded ellRd) + C_{ν,R}(S) τ + ε`.
- **Prose**: rounding the prime endpoints to cells of width τ changes the sieve cost by `O(τ)`. This follows from Mertens-type prime harmonic sums.
- **Source**: V22.
- **Mapping**: the cell width `τ` and the endpoints `wτ` are parameters. `CnuR S` is defined in V22.
- **Effectivity**: effective in principle.

## 3. `euler : PrincipalEulerProvider h r Sd LF I (S0 τC W) N Li phiW model`
- **Lean**: this field is data plus properties. `euler_product : Zgen M s t = excLocal M s t · ∏_{p ∈ good M} eulerFactor p r s t`;
  `zeta_simple_pole` (provable: `zeta_simple_pole_available`); `mellin_truncation`; `mixed_derivative : |mellin M · log^r M − (Sall/Sij)·LF| ≤ ε` eventually;
  `normalization_agreement : S0Contract (S0 τC W) N`; `sifted_main : |model.sifted(pref) − Si (Sij/Si)(Sall/Sij)/Sall · gConst · (LF/I)| ≤ ε` eventually.
- **Prose**: the principal second moment is evaluated through its Euler product and a truncated Mellin integral. The zeroth moment `S0` is asymptotic to `N`.
- **Source**: V23 `PrincipalEulerProvider`, and the V23 report.
- **Mapping**: `S0 τC W` is **defined** (V16 `RouteCConsumer.S0`: the weighted window count of the physical source). `N`, `model`, `Li` and `phiW` are parameters.
- **Normalization**: the same `N` as in S1, pref, the pair baseline and the consumer (`same_normalization_end_to_end`).
- **Effectivity**: ineffective as stated (ε/eventual form).

## 4. `hat : HatReferenceApproximationProvider Kh EAB`
- **Lean**: `nonneg : ∀ M, 0 ≤ EAB M`; `bound : ∃ C ≥ 0, ∃ M₀, ∀ M ≥ M₀, EAB M ≤ C / log M ^ (Kh + 26)`.
- **Prose**: the tensor / hat reference approximation error saves `log^{-(K+26)}`.
- **Source**: V23 `HatApproximationProvider`.
- **Mapping**: `EAB` is a parameter, and it is not defined from the source.
- **Effectivity**: ineffective as stated.

## 5. `di : DISpectralProvider (1/1100) DIClass`
- **Lean**: `spectral : ∀ K : KloostermanData, DIClass K → MaynardAdmissible (1/1100) K → DIConclusion K`, where
  `DIConclusion K := 0 ≤ Ξ ∧ (∀ c supported off-diagonal, ‖Σ_b Σ_z c(z) Kl(b;z)‖ ≤ x^{ε_DI} Ξ ‖c‖₂) ∧ mass·Ξ·√Rep ≤ N_q² T √(Δ₂+Δ₃)`.
- **Prose**: this is the Deshouillers–Iwaniec bound for sums of Kloosterman sums, in Maynard's normalization with ε_DI = η/4 and η = 1/1100.
- **Source**: V27 `DISpectralProvider`.
- **Variable / range mapping**: `MaynardAdmissible` is the literal §5.2 range condition. It is defined.
- **Coefficient mapping**: `c` is supported on the off-diagonal set.
- **Class**: **`DIClass` is undefined.** The field is vacuous for the empty class and false for the full class (`DIClass_underdetermined`). The arithmetic §4 conditions alone also make it false (`arithOnlyClass_provider_false`). The kernel is load-bearing (`kernel_is_load_bearing`). Until DIClass is defined as the literal public DI class, this field cannot be matched to the published theorem.
- **Effectivity**: effective in principle (spectral large sieve). The exceptional-eigenvalue dependence is not tracked.

## 6. `zeroFreq : BranchClassBound Us Ur D0`
- **Lean**: `linear : D0 M (Σ c_i g_i) = Σ c_i D0 M g_i`; `class_bound : ∀ S, ∀ ε>0, ∃ M₀, ∀ M ≥ M₀, ∀ g, SourceFactorization g (Us S M) (Ur S M) → |D0 M g| ≤ ε`.
- **Prose**: masked Siegel–Walfisz / Barban–Davenport–Halberstam for weights of the shape `g ⋆ h`, where both factors are one-bounded and supported on the sieve universes.
- **Source**: V28, plus V25 (`zero_frequency_localized_bound`, which holds for an explicit `FullSum`).
- **Mapping**: `D0` is a **parameter**, not linked to the V25 `FullSum` or to the physical source. `SourceFactorization` is defined (V22).
- **Effectivity**: ineffective (Siegel).

## 7. `oneLarge : BranchClassBound Us Ur D1`
- Same shape as field 6, for the one-large Heath-Brown branch. `D1` is a parameter. **No literal one-large analytic theorem with sequence, modulus and coefficient hypotheses exists in the repository.** The external statement therefore cannot be checked beyond this class-bound shape.

## 8. `twoLarge : BranchClassBound Us Ur D2`
- The same as field 7, for the two-large branch.

## 9. `boundary : BranchClassBound Us Ur Db`
- Same shape as field 6, for the product-boundary contribution. The budget arithmetic is in V26 `BoundaryBudget`. `Db` is a parameter.

## 10. `s1 : S1Contract (S1 τC W) N muF`
- **Lean**: `∀ η > 0, ∃ M₀, ∀ M ≥ M₀, μ_F − η ≤ S1 M / N M`.
- **Prose**: this is the first-moment asymptotic (prime count over the window). It is Bombieri–Vinogradov type.
- **Source**: V14/V15 (`s1_contract`, which is conditional on `OrdinaryBVProvider`).
- **Mapping**: `S1 τC W` is **defined** (V16 `RouteCConsumer.S1`). `N` is the common normalization.
- **Effectivity**: ineffective (BV / Siegel).

---

## Not in the minimal bundle (for completeness)

- `FunctionalKernelCertificate muF WF`. This is a FINITE CERTIFIED INPUT: `7147687/10000 < μ_F`, `W_F < 98278402/10000`, `0 ≤ W_F`. Its provenance is `certificateProvenance`. No certificate data exists in the repository.
- `InternalGlueOwner`. This is INTERNAL and was not eliminated: the fields `tensor` and `nonzero`, as in `PROVIDER_CLASSIFICATION.md`.

# Merikoski v3 ↔ fixed-affine W2.984 dictionary

Sources: J. Merikoski, arXiv:1811.03008v3 [M]; Banks–Freiberg–Maynard arXiv:1404.5094v2 [BFM];
Polymath8b arXiv:1407.4897v4 [PM]. Section numbers (§) refer to `AFFINE_CHEN_TRANSFER_W2984.md`.

## Notation

| Merikoski (shifts) | fixed affine (W2.984) |
|---|---|
| \(n\in(N,2N]\), \(n\equiv b\ (W)\) | \(t\in\mathcal T=(T_1,T_2]\cap(t_0+W\mathbb Z)\) |
| \(n+h_i\) | \(L_i(t)=a_it+1\), \(a_i\le H\) distinct |
| \(P^+(\prod(h_j-h_i))\le\epsilon\log N\) | \(P^+(\prod a_i\prod(a_i-a_k))\le H<\epsilon\log X\) (§1.3) |
| \(\frac NW B^{-K}L_K(F)\) | \(\mathfrak M=\#\mathcal T\,B^{-K}L_K(F)\) |
| \(\nu_{\mathcal H,j,\ell}\) (with the \(Z\)-factor) | \(\nu_{j\ell}\) (without the \(Z\)-factor; Remark 8.3) |
| \(P(Y)\), \(P_0(Y)\) | \(P_{\mathcal P}(Y)\) with \(\mathcal P\) = primes \(\ne Z_{\rm exc}\) |
| \(y_1=\exp(\log^{1/3}N)\), \(y_2=N^{\delta^2}\), \(\varrho\), \(G\) | \(y=\exp((\log X)^{1/3})\), \(z_0=X^{\delta^2}\), \(\rho\), \(H\) (§4) |

## Results

| Merikoski v3 | Fixed-affine W2.984 | Changed? | Nature | Proof location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lemma 13 (Chen inequality) | Lemma 2.1 / 2.2, affine Chen decomposition + \(S_{\rm sq}\) | **yes**: the pointwise inequality is false for non-squarefree \(n\) (kernel counterexample \(n=1925\)); corrected by \(\frac12\mathrm{sq}(n)\) | new correction; combinatorics independent of affine setting | §2; Lean `chen_pointwise`, `chen_weighted`, `affine_chen_weighted`, `merikoski_pointwise_fails` |
| — | Lemma 10.1 `AffineSquareTail` | new | new (elementary) | §10 |
| Lemma 14 (linear sieve) | same | no | citation [FI, Ch. 11–12] | §7.2, §8.4 |
| Lemma 15 (\(S_1\)) | Lemma 7.1 `AffineChenS1` | **yes**: literal CRT system for \(p=L_j(t)\), base \(a_jW\), \(\phi(a_jW)=a_j\phi(W)\), remainder classification (a)–(e) | new derivation, same main term | §3, §7 |
| Lemma 16 (\(S_2\)) | Lemma 8.1 `AffineChenS2` | **yes**: as Lemma 15, plus a two-sided small-prime split; \(p\) never overlaps spectators (\(p>X^\delta\)) | new derivation, same main term | §8 |
| Lemma 17 (\(S_3\)) | Lemma 9.1 `AffineChenS3` | **yes**: switch \(x=L_\ell(t)\), \(L_j=(a_jx+a_\ell-a_j)/a_\ell\), non-squarefree base \(a_\ell W\), exceptional prime in \(s\) (Remark 9.4) | new derivation, same main term | §9 |
| Prop 8 = [BFM, Thm 4.2] | Lemma 6.1 (primes) | **proof re-verified**: conductor \(W\)-part \(a'\mid aW\) instead of \(a'\mid q_0\) | statement cited; proof modifications listed (steps 1–9) | §6 |
| Prop 11 (BV for almost-primes) | Lemma 6.1 (\(\Lambda_0\)) | **proof re-verified** as above; support hypotheses checked for the switched source | statement cited; proof modifications listed | §6, §9.4 |
| §6 "Lemma 21" (exceptional set, \(1_{(n,P_0(y_1))=1}=\varrho+O(\tau^2\psi)\)) | Lemma 4.1 | written two-sided: \(0\le\rho-1\le\tau^2\psi\) | rederived | §4.1 |
| §6 "Lemma 22" (smooth numbers) | Lemma 4.2 | affine count \(\#\{t:e\mid L_\ell(t)\}\le\#\mathcal T/e+1\); decay \(\exp(-c\delta^2(\log X)^{2/3})\) | rederived; \(\Psi(x,y)\ll xe^{-u/2}\) cited | §4.2 |
| §6 overlap bound \(N\log^{O(1)}/(Wy_1^{1/2})\) | Lemma 4.3 | same exponent \(y^{-1/2}\); affine count via (A1) | rederived | §4.3 |
| §6 generalised Polymath lemma (Euler evaluation) | Lemma 4.4 | pairwise coprimality derived from distinct affine roots (A2); local factors \(1/\phi(q)\) (Lemma 3.6) | lemma cited; the reduction to its hypotheses is new | §4.4 |
| (main) evaluation \((1+o(1))\frac NW B^{-K+1}L_K\) | Lemma 3.5 + 4.4 | slope cancels: \(\pi(I_j)/\phi(a_jW)=(1+o(1))\#\mathcal TB^{-1}\) | new bookkeeping | §3, §4.4 |
| Proposition 12 (\(3.99\)) | Theorem 11.1 (\(c_{\rm cert}+C_{\rm err}\delta\)) | yes (affine source; constant sharpened to \(<3.984\)) | combination kernel-checked (`pairExpect_le_chen`) | §11 |
| numerics \(\Omega_1\le4.19\), \(\Omega_2\ge0.279\), \(\Omega_3\le0.076\) | \(\Omega_1-\Omega_2+\Omega_3\le3.983412536315\) | yes | kernel-checked | §12 |

**Previous verdicts:** `W3: PASS`; `W2.984: REPAIR — expository, not mathematical`.

and affine analogues of the \(S_1,S_2,S_3\) estimates to be written in full. These are now in

   \(n\) (kernel counterexample \(n=1925\)). It is repaired by adding \(\frac12\mathrm{sq}(n)\);
   the resulting tail is negligible (§10). The constant is unaffected. Please check that this
   repair is acceptable.

# Audit: the Chen / P₂ relaxation of the blocker pair (Erdős #287 kernel)

Audit only. No claim that #287 is solved. Every machine-checked claim below is a theorem
in `RequestProject/Erdos287/ChenP2Audit.lean`; the file builds and contains no `sorry`,
`axiom`, `unsafe`, or `native_decide`, and every cited theorem reduces to the allowed
axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.

## The question

In the certified kernel, the blocker-pair contradiction (`Gap2CE.excludedPP_blockerPair`)
forces two adjacent holes `x, x+1 ∈ [N, M]` from two **excluded prime powers** `q₁ ∣ x`,
`q₂ ∣ x+1`. Exclusion is delivered by `primePower_window_exclusion`. Can **one** side be
relaxed from a prime power `q` to a `P₂ = q₁·q₂` (semiprime) while still forcing its hole?

## Task 1 — the exact relaxed statements

* `IsP2 q` — `q` is a product of two primes.
* `ExcludedP2Naive M q` — the literal analogue of `ExcludedPP`, in its **most favourable**
  form: `q = p₁·p₂` (`p₁ ≤ p₂`), window `⌊M/q⌋`, threshold `C(⌊M/q⌋) < p₁`. (Smallest
  possible window ⇒ smallest `C`; only the smaller factor must beat it. If this cannot
  force exclusion, no weaker P₂ rule can.)
* `P2ForcesExclusion` — the relaxed exclusion primitive: a naively-excluded `P₂` avoids
  every reciprocal-sum-`1` set `A ⊆ [1,M]` (analogue of `ExcludedPP.not_dvd_mem`).
* `RelaxedBlockerPair` — the relaxed blocker-pair theorem: one side `ExcludedP2Naive`, the
  other `ExcludedPP`, forcing `False` on a `Gap2CE`.

## Task 2 — attempt to prove it

The proof of `primePower_window_exclusion` is intrinsically single-prime: divisibility by
`p^e` places the element in the **top `p`-adic layer**, whose reciprocal-sum numerator is
`≤ C(⌊M/p^e⌋)` yet `≡ 0 (mod p)` (`topLayer_congruence`), forcing it to vanish once
`p > C(⌊M/p^e⌋)`. A semiprime supplies **no single modulus** with a dominant valuation, so
there is nothing to run the top-layer congruence against. The relaxation cannot be proved.

## Task 3 — it is false, with a concrete local configuration

`not_P2ForcesExclusion : ¬ P2ForcesExclusion`.

Concrete configuration: `A = {2, 3, 6}`, `∑ 1/a = 1` (`p2_witness_sum`), `M = 6`, semiprime
`q = 6 = 2·3`.

* `p2_six_excludedNaive : ExcludedP2Naive 6 6` — the *product* window is `⌊6/6⌋ = 1`, and
  `C 1 = 1 < 2`, so the naive P₂ rule **predicts a hole at 6**.
* But `6 ∈ A`, so **no hole is forced** — the prediction is wrong.

`p2_window_illegitimate` explains why: the top-layer argument only ever provides the window
of an *individual* prime factor `pᵢ`, `⌊M/pᵢ⌋`, never the smaller product window `⌊M/q⌋`.
For both factors of `6` the legitimate window fails to exclude:

* factor `2`: `⌊6/2⌋ = 3`, `C 3 = 11 ≥ 2`;
* factor `3`: `⌊6/3⌋ = 2`, `C 2 = 3 ≥ 3`.

The fallacy of the relaxation is exactly the illegitimate replacement `⌊M/pᵢ⌋ ↝ ⌊M/q⌋`.

## Salvage (not a genuine relaxation)

`P2_excluded_via_prime_factor`: if one prime factor `p₀ ∣ q` is *itself* an excluded prime
power (`ExcludedPP M p₀`), then `q` forces a hole — but only because `p₀ ∣ x` already does,
via `ExcludedPP.not_dvd_mem`. This is the prime-power blocker in disguise and gains nothing:
it needs the *larger* factor to be a near-`M` prime, i.e. it is not a P₂ relaxation at all.

## Task 4 — Chen-type input gives no usable infinite tail

A Chen-type theorem (infinitely many primes `p` with `p+2` a `P₂`) supplies infinitely many
`(prime, P₂)` neighbours. Turning them into a tail of blocker pairs needs each `P₂` to force
its hole, i.e. it needs `RelaxedBlockerPair` / `P2ForcesExclusion`. Since these are false
(`chen_no_usable_tail = not_P2ForcesExclusion`), the prime side gives one hole and the `P₂`
side gives none: no adjacent double hole is produced, so **no usable infinite tail** follows
through this mechanism.

Because the P₂ relaxation fails, the sound blocker inputs remain the genuine prime-power
pairs already certified (`Gap2CE.excludedPP_blockerPair`, and the good-prime / safe-prime
blockers `Gap2CE.goodPrime_blocker_{sub,add}`, `Gap2CE.safePrime_blocker`, which do require
a genuinely large prime factor rather than a mere almost-prime).

## Required output

* **Can one side be relaxed to P₂?** No — not by the top-layer / prime-power exclusion
  theorem. The relaxation is false.
* **First point of failure.** The exclusion primitive `P2ForcesExclusion`
  (`not_P2ForcesExclusion`), i.e. the illegitimate window replacement `⌊M/pᵢ⌋ ↝ ⌊M/q⌋`
  (`p2_window_illegitimate`).
* **Concrete counterexample.** `A = {2,3,6}`, `M = 6`, `q = 6 = 2·3`.
* **Theorems (in `ChenP2Audit.lean`).** `IsP2`, `ExcludedP2Naive`, `P2ForcesExclusion`,
  `RelaxedBlockerPair`, `p2_witness_sum`, `p2_six_excludedNaive`, `not_P2ForcesExclusion`,
  `p2_window_illegitimate`, `P2_excluded_via_prime_factor`, `chen_no_usable_tail`.
* **Build.** Succeeds (`RequestProject.Main`, 8040 jobs).
* **Placeholders.** None; only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` are used.

# Erdős #287 — non-adjacent holes and the Kernel AP-blocker

This note answers two follow-up questions on the certified gap-`≤2` kernel. Everything
below is machine-checked (no `sorry`/`axiom`/`unsafe`/`native_decide`); every listed
theorem depends only on `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.

The certified adjacent-hole fact is `Gap2CE.blockerPair_contradiction`: two holes at
distance **1** in `[N, M]` contradict all gaps `≤ 2`. This is the *only* pattern the
gap constraint forbids, because the constraint (`Gap2CE.holes_isolated`, symbolically
`LocallyAdmissible`) is a nearest-neighbour subshift whose single forbidden 2-block is
`(hole, hole)`.

## Part A — Do two holes at distance `d > 1` force a contradiction?

**Verdict: No.** No non-adjacent-hole contradiction survives at the level used by
`blockerPair_contradiction`. For every distance `d ≥ 2` there is an explicit locally
admissible configuration exhibiting two holes exactly at distance `d`; since
`blockerPair_contradiction` is derived purely from the local gap rule, no distance-`d`
analogue can hold. Only `d = 1` is inadmissible.

File: `RequestProject/Erdos287/NonAdjacentHoles.lean`.

### Target 1 — prove or refute (refuted)

* `twoHoleWord x d` — the membership word with holes exactly at `x` and `x + d`.
* `twoHoleWord_locallyAdmissible (x) (hd : 2 ≤ d)` — for `d ≥ 2` this word satisfies the
  local gap rule. **This refutes the distance-`d` contradiction claim.**
* `twoHoleWord_has_two_holes` — the two prescribed holes are genuinely present.
* `twoHoleWord_one_not_admissible` — the sharp contrast: `d = 1` (adjacency) is *not*
  admissible. Adjacency is the unique local contradiction.
* `no_nonadjacent_local_contradiction (hd : 2 ≤ d) (x)` — packaged negative answer: a
  locally admissible word with holes at `x` and `x + d` exists for every `d ≥ 2`.
* `distance_band_admissible` — the whole requested band `d ∈ {2, …, 246}` is covered.

### Target 2 — explicit local gap patterns

The word `twoHoleWord x d` *is* the explicit local model: positions `x` and `x + d` are
holes, every other position is in `A`, and (for `d ≥ 2`) no two holes are adjacent, so all
gaps are `≤ 2`. For example at `d = 2`: `…, x-1∈A, x=hole, x+1∈A, x+2=hole, x+3∈A, …`.

### Target 3 — stronger variants (all compatible, none force a contradiction)

* **A block of many forced holes in a short interval.** `many_holes_block k` produces `k`
  holes of the alternating word inside `[0, 2k]`; with `k = 123` that is 123 forced holes
  inside an interval of length 246, none adjacent (`altWord_block_locallyAdmissible`,
  `altWord_holes_nonadjacent`). The densest admissible hole set is an entire parity class.
* **Both parity classes densely.** `mod3HoleWord` (holes at every multiple of 3) hits both
  parities (`mod3HoleWord_both_parities`) yet is admissible
  (`mod3HoleWord_locallyAdmissible`).
* **`gcd`-controlled endpoints.** `gcd_controlled_models` gives admissible witnesses with
  both coprime endpoints (`gcd 6 11 = 1`) and non-coprime endpoints (`gcd 6 12 = 6`);
  admissibility does not depend on `gcd(x, x+d)`.
* **The arithmetic mechanism cannot close either.** `exists_crt_at_distance` shows the
  CRT machinery can *produce* two hole-forcing multiples at any prescribed distance `d ≥ 1`
  (given `Q₁·Q₂ + d ≤ M − N + 1`, `gcd(Q₁,Q₂)=1`). For `d = 1` this is exactly the adjacent
  input of `blockerPair_contradiction`; for `d ≥ 2` the two holes are non-adjacent, so no
  contradiction follows. Producing distance-`d` holes is possible; concluding `False` is
  not.

### Target 4 — output

* Exact theorem names: as listed above.
* Does any non-adjacent-hole contradiction survive? **No.**
* Counterexamples / local models: `twoHoleWord` (distance `d`), `altWord` (dense block /
  one parity), `mod3HoleWord` (both parities). All are `LocallyAdmissible`.

## Part B — the Kernel AP-blocker

This is a genuine *adjacent*-hole blocker packaged from an arithmetic-progression input.

File: `RequestProject/Erdos287/KernelAPBlocker.lean`.

Setup: `A ⊆ [N, M]` a `Gap2CE`, `M ≥ 8152`; for a prime `p`, `qₚ = p^(eₚ+1)` (`ceilMod`).
Kernel modulus `Qₚ` (`Gap2CE.kernelMod p`): `q₂` for `p = 2`, and `2·qₚ` for odd `p`.

* `Gap2CE.HoleForcing.of_dvd` — hole-forcing is upward closed under divisibility.
* `Gap2CE.ceilMod_dvd_kernelMod`, `Gap2CE.one_le_kernelMod`,
  `Gap2CE.kernelMod_holeForcing` — `qₚ ∣ Qₚ`, `Qₚ ≥ 1`, and `Qₚ` is hole-forcing.
* `Gap2CE.AP_prime_kills_holeForcing_add` — the `+1` companion of the existing
  `AP_prime_kills_holeForcing`.
* `Gap2CE.kernel_AP_blocker` — **no prime `r ∈ [N+1, M−1]` has `r ≡ ±1 (mod Qₚ)`**
  (stated as `Qₚ ∣ (r−1) ∨ Qₚ ∣ (r+1)`).
* `Gap2CE.kernel_AP_blocker_modEq` — the same statement with literal congruences
  `r ≡ 1` / `r ≡ Qₚ − 1 (mod Qₚ)`.

Reason: `Qₚ ∣ (r∓1)` gives `qₚ ∣ (r∓1)`, so `r∓1` is a ceiling hole; `r` is a prime hole
(`primeFree`). The two are adjacent, contradicting `blockerPair_contradiction`.
